body.title: Police?  Stop Wasting Taxpayers' Money On Your Moral Crusades!
body.body: ![FsHH is the author of this picture/Source: Pixabay](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2017/07/06/23/33/man-2479882_1280.jpg) The other day I came across a video on the Law&Crime Network channel on YouTube. I'm not a major fan of that same YouTube channel. However, this one news story caught my attention. A 19-year-old daycare worker got caught kissing a 5-year-old girl on the lips multiple times. Below is the video about it. A 19-Year-Old Man Was Arrested For Kissing A 5-Year-Old Girl On The Lips More Than Once https://youtu.be/M6pA4_-OYj0?si=xn-tsLiaxSOvMmzd So here we have a man over the legal age of majority making moves on a defenseless, little girl whom he is supposed to be caring for and protecting. He was caught with pornographic contraband on his computer that showed small children in sexually explicit images. This same young man is about as guilty as guilty gets for sex crimes against children. We can only hope that he will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. You have to question if the daycare center even performed any kind of background check on him. I guess the downside of this same suspect being so young is that if he committed sex crimes against small children when he was still a minor, then his police record would likely have been expunged on his eighteenth birthday. I'm not one hundred percent sure about how the laws pertaining to juvenile records work in Ohio. Now, here is the point that I'd like to make about this news story. Law-enforcement officials waste so much time and tax dollars chasing after 18- and 19-year-old men who perhaps may be dating a 14- or 15-year-old girl. Police get eager to participate in online sex-sting operations that are teenage-pregnancy-prevent campaigns at best rather than genuine efforts to stop child molestation and sex crimes against children. If there are 18- and 19-year-old men committing heinous sex crimes against 5-year-old girls, why do the authorities need to be investigating liaisons in which a teenage adult man and a teenage minor girl are each slightly on opposite sides of the legal age line? A police officer's time and the taxpayers' money could be better spent going after teenage adult men like the one in the news story above. What Chris Hansen has done for a living all these years is merely an attempt to sensationalize on Americans' insecurities over teenage girls having sex at young ages with partners outside their own peer circles. He hasn't been saving anyone from harm. There are not even any victims involved in his online sex-sting operations except for the young men that he entraps. In television interviews, Mr. Hansen has flapped his jaws about how he feels it's important that he entraps 18- and 19-year-old young men who may show a non-Platonic interest in adolescent girls between 13 and 15 years of age. However, those young men are not a threat to society. The former 19-year-old daycare worker in the video above is. So what if a 14-year-old girl has her parents fooled into believing that her 19-year-old boyfriend is only 15 years old? If something bad is going to happen to her in a relationship with a man five years older than her, it's going to happen to her with a boy her own age. However, when a 19-year-old man is kissing a 5-year-old girl on the lips and taking every opportunity to be alone with her, you have to suspect that his intentions are less than wholesome, to say the least. A 14-year-old girl can back out of a relationship with an older boyfriend any time that she wishes to do so. In many countries, a 14-year-old girl is considered to be a consenting adult under their laws. On the other hand, a 5-year-old girl has no idea what a 19-year-old man is planning to do to her once he starts engaging in questionable behavior with her. That 19-year-old man can do a significant amount of damage to that little girl. A 5-year-old girl cannot consent to anything depraved that a 19-year-old man does to her, because she doesn't have the ability to attain a full understanding of what is being done to her other than that it feels horrible once it happens. Our criminal justice system needs to get out of its make-believe world of age-appropriate perfection and wholesome purity and do a reality check on what the real crimes against children involve. While police officials are entrapping adult men in online sex-sting operations for attempting to hook up with teenage minors that don't even exist, real child molesters and predatory pedophiles are sexually victimizing small children under 11 years old that are in vulnerable positions. American statutory-rape laws pertaining to teenage minors are not really helping anyone other than angry parents that want revenge on a college student who got their 15-year-old girl pregnant unintentionally. Meanwhile, there are adult men and women of all ages in positions of trust and authority that are preying on small children in daycare centers and the likes, and child molesters are getting away with it inasmuch as they know that nobody is watching them. It needs to stop. ![The author of this picture is unlisted/Source: Pixabay](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2013/05/14/18/08/police-officer-111116_1280.jpg) So what if John Walsh doesn't differentiate between child molesters that prey on toddlers and young adult men in college that date teenage girls in high school and even middle school? Like Chris Hansen and Oprah Winfrey, he's an out-of-touch baby boomer that cannot get all his facts straight about child predation and pedophilia. These three people have their heads in the clouds. **This article is copyright-protected.**

body.title: Stunning Fungi At My Parent's Frontyard!
body.body:
The old Udara (African star apple) tree in my parent’s front yard seems to be saying, “No more fruits? No stress. Here — have some golden-orange mushrooms for your viewing pleasure instead.” Lol. 

Every rainy season, this dead Udara log transforms. What was once a dry wood then becomes an apartment for various kinds of mushrooms. 

Last season, it housed Scaly Lentinus and a few other inedible mushrooms. This season, the log sprouted clusters of yellow-orange mushrooms instead, so bright you'd be tempted to forage for them and afterwards, prepare *creamy mushroom soup, mushroom ragu or even the classic garlic butter sautéed mushrooms.*  Unfortunately, they're inedible. Hehehe. 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaJ1GU84iykvNrH81TvHAkg5nvU74saYbgLgZidEcWKBX/1777048424781.jpg)




The log is just beside my mom's small farm, and I'd gone to check out the fresh ridges she just made, that's when I spotted the mushrooms.
A search identified the mushroom as the \

, and are known to grow in clusters on dead or decaying wood. 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSs32hAgwdB2mi1cm2yUtHt2gARNCfxEayL3s1H6SgbDz/1777048424187.jpg)
***


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPCJ8Mzzse4Bj671ohpxwmRqKyTgG4WKkLv9VXL7hoWLQ/1777048424935.jpg)



***



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdmRjyXxLhAa76AZDHck65rY89sqEQEXHYFEkkmKGpYU8/1777048470241.jpg)


Although they're not typically considered deadly, but it's best to avoid consuming them. Some of these wild mushrooms can be toxic. 




![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYrx2Y1y9GgmHvzh7Yy71q378kuAcui7Zg4h9B2Zwm4N2/1777048425103.jpg)

Honestly, I wished they were edible, would foraged for them and prepared mushroom soup with Achara (edible elephant grass) and uziza leaves. 


These one are almost rotten. See how the color is. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQnrmw6LY8pwbW2NcZyVcxMM9afG7WVh2rxTC5upHYg2D/1777048470019.jpg)

Well, I captured them to share with you, and I'd love to know if you've come across this type of mushroom before.

body.title: Book Review - Bronze Age Military Equipment by Dan Howard
body.body:
Last week I reviewed [**Chariot by Arthur Cottrell**](https://peakd.com/hive-180164/@alonicus/book-review-chariot-by-arthur-cotterell), a book covering one of the most iconic aspects of Bronze Age warfare. I found it to be a great read, but flawed in a number of ways.

So this time, I'm reviewing the next book I read on Bronze Age warfare. This covers the equipment used, and the author is both an historian and a gamer, with a strong interest in martial arts and re-enactment. It makes a difference !

![IMG_20260418_103652.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alonicus/23xySqPsPL4HHidJigafjiyy8MuVXZMEsdGN57dtfPDbQcNxNG44B86X4Sz6MMXiodpun.jpg)


![Hive Divider3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alonicus/243C5mWFmzYKkxg4arJr6HtnfHGJpnth33F4sSek1XxEQS3vHpdjcuokqyKGz3jFHfMZf.jpg)

At first glance, this book appears as a very dry reference tome, the kind of thing that you use to look up a specific topic rather than read from cover to cover.

Compared to Chariot, I was immediately struck by the far more structured and logical layout of the book. It is divided into five chapters each dealing with a specific topic, as well as four appendices and the normal index, lists of plates, sources etc.

The chapters start with one covering Bronze Age warfare, which demonstrates how it evolved over the period, what social and material changes led to that evolution, and a lot (and I mean a LOT !) of references to original evidence to back each assertion up. As with all the chapters, it is nicely divided by logical sub-headings to further segment the information.

Following this chapter, the succeeding ones cover weapons, chariots, armour and shields. Again, the same rigorous logic is followed, with each chapter looking at carefully-sourced geographical variations in the same order. Compared to Arthur Cotterell's book, the structure and clarity is a stand-out feature.

Something which I found particularly interesting when it came to the armour and shield chapters was that where possible, reference was made to experimental archaeology, understanding in depth how historical replicas of the protective gear were constructed and behaved when confronting the weapons of the time.

Too often I've seen television documentaries doing incredibly poor experimental archaeology, making a replica shield out of plywood, testing it against steel-headed modern arrows and declaring it to be of no protective value.

This book doesn't do that. The replicas are constructed as close as possible to originals that have been excavated, and tested against authentic weaponry. The tests are outlined with actual statistics, detailing how deeply weapons penetrated the armour etc.

I particularly like the recognition that most archers continued to use flint arrows well into the Bronze Age; they were surprisingly effective against flesh, textiles and wood, only really struggling against bronze armour that would have been \

and very expensive for the time period. I also like that the author points out any issues with the testing, for example that the thickness of reconstructed armour may not be correct due to the originals having been buried for a few thousand years and possibly suffering from corrosion.

The appendices were a big surprise to me. Too often, the appendices of a book are eminently skippable. Either they are just lists of sources, or sometimes tables of data. In this case, each of the four appendices is a deep dive into a specific sub-topic that might have been included in overview in the main text but are worthy of further detail.

The first appendix looks at Homeric shields, covering the detailed evidence presented both in the Iliad and archaology of the different types of shield and how they are likely to have been used. This is then used to construct a replica of Hector's shield from the siege of Troy. It goes into serious detail, even including how the the bronze outer layer became thinner towards the edge, how that affected the overall weight and how the shield would have behaved in combat.

The second appendix covers armour in similar depth, and I have to mention the plate included in the book of the incredible replica of the Dendra panoply the author owns. I've seen the original in Napflion Museum, and that is impressive enough, but the replica is just awesome.



![IMG_20260418_103708.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alonicus/23yTizanFEbdPbQG4SNnNNigx58ApADvEVG7eugZNZLyvhuMfPzaHDSjAbRAcaMiu8YFq.jpg)

It is interesting that Dan Howard reaches a far more nuanced conclusion than Arthur Cotterell when it comes to this armour. In Chariot, Arthur Cotterell dances around how and when this armour was used, and concludes by calling it \

. Dan Howard is clear that the use of this type of heavy armour had been abandoned by the time of the siege of Troy, due to changes in the way warfare was conducted, but that in an earlier period when the key threat was from chariot archers, it would have been essential for an armoured chariot driver. Unlike the archer, the driver was less able to dodge or duck, and if he was hit the whole chariot would be lost, so he needed protecting. By the time of Troy, infantry were more disciplined and better armoured, so the chariot archer was far less effective.

The third appendix is a useful round up of what warriors from each geographical location would have looked like, and the differences between them. A useful summary !

Finally, appendix 4 is a wonderfully illustrated typology of Bronze Age European and Middle Eastern swords. It's a great reference source. If I ever come into enough money to be able to afford one of Brian Burridge's incredible museum quality replicas, this will be like my shopping list !

Overall, this is one of the best books I've read on any early military historical subject. I kind of wish there were more line illustrations, but that's a very minor nit-pick. The book is packed with detail, and the explanations and layout are clear enough that it makes the whole thing a fascinating and easy read. For anyone interested in the Bronze Age, it's a \

that should be on your bookshelf, especially if you want to understand it from a re-enactment or experimental archaeology perspective. The volume of sources could probably give you a lifetime's reading and research. 


![Hive Divider3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alonicus/243C5mWFmzYKkxg4arJr6HtnfHGJpnth33F4sSek1XxEQS3vHpdjcuokqyKGz3jFHfMZf.jpg)

*Photos are by me, of my copy of the book.*

Published in 2011 by Pen and Sword Books Ltd. 169 pages with 15 plates. ISBN 1399023373

body.body:

<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/shiftrox/23xybSfh9YqAWCc4CM2LpTQW7s5C6BbtGnbbVBbTbYtFE8F2SXcUDUsFAWGzgBeSyx5Cm.png)[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/pt-br/fotografias/duas-pessoas-em-pe-na-pavimentacao-de-telha-cinza-TamMbr4okv4)</center>

Hard work isn't always rewarded, but that doesn't mean you shouldn't do your best. Many who try don't succeed, but those who succeed certainly tried, and that's the idea I have for myself. It's not easy and it never will be, but giving up on every dream isn't the right thing to do. Something has to work out, and for that, we'll keep trying as many times as necessary to reach our goal.

I'm developing something that might not even yield results, but that doesn't scare me. Putting effort into something you enjoy, creating, tinkering, changing—why wouldn't we like that? Not everything needs to be profitable (at least not at the beginning), but what about the passion for creating content? For creating the pieces? The universe? Man, I know it's not easy investing our precious time in things we love if they don't yield results, but does it always have to be like that? Definitely not!

In my mind, some things have to be like this: passion and love, doing it because you believe in it, period, screw the result. Of course, if there's something you want at the end of all this and you manage to achieve it, great, but what if there isn't? It's not the end; you tried, you did your best, you grew, you learned, and that's it, everything becomes experience to do better later. Dive headfirst into something that is your dream and, with that, ignore the criticism, those who work against you, and just do it!

Taking your dream out of the drawer is one of the best things we can do. You have no idea how many things I've kept hidden, and now, with the help of AI, my mind and ideas, being executed by them, are becoming reality.

Of course, people will criticize you, they'll say things like \

, so, just one question: the architect who designs a project isn't the person who lays the bricks, yet they usually get the credit, right? But what about the bricklayers? What about the foreman? What about everyone involved in building this project in the real world? What is this project worth on paper? ***Right or wrong doesn't exist when you have the passion to make it happen!*** ![sun_divisor.webp](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXEDLx7R7Jy8fHF1tA7sPyb4A9QBvmj3y4FjFhephcPCS/sun_divisor.webp)

To explain what is going on mathematically:

This is the model of a state machine.  A state machine transitions through states according to the rules and invariants. Model checking, or state machines, are about the relationships between the states. What we can do, is decide which states are safe to reach, and which states are disaster states which must be unreachable.

The disaster set D ⊆ Q contains every state the protocol must never reach. 

The way to mathematically guarantee the software only behaves as intended, is to make the disaster states unreachable:

body.title: The Man at Table Seven
body.body:
It wasn't a fancy place.

One of those cafes people went to think, or use their laptop, or just sometimes sit and do nothing. It had soft music and those lights that made it feel like time was passing more slowly than it was.

Ada used to go there a lot.

Same seat. Same corner. Same routine.

One day he came.

He came in, like he was lost. He was dressed simply, a little bit old, not new, not fresh. He was carrying a black bag, old, worn, well used.

He stood outside for a while, looking about.

And then he sat down at Table Seven.

Alone.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXDSz919bFWp92YYNeFRBzCFVfrHMySbttH85o3s6hpFo/1777056516837.png)


It wasnt long before he noticed him.

The waiter approached cautiously.

“Good afternoon, sir. What would you like?”

The man hesitated before answering. “Just tea.”

Just tea.

That was enough to get some judgements started.

Ada overheard the girls at the next table to hers.

\

“Or he might be waiting for someone to buy him.”

They laughed quietly.

Ada didn’t laugh.

She looked over again.

But he was there and he was quiet. Like he wasn't really there.



A couple of times the next few days he came back.

Same time. Same table. Same order.

Tea.

No phone. No laptop. No distractions.

Just silence.

He started attracting attention to himself but not for the right reasons.

\

another said.

Even people like waitresses and checkers began to react to him differently; not rudely, but not so friendly as they were to others.

Ada observed all this.

It was all different that day.

It was just another day. He arrived, ordered his usual cup of tea and sat at Table Seven.

But on this day, just over 30 minutes later, a child walked in.

After looking about, he approached the man.

\

The man smiled.

It was the first time she had ever seen him smile.

\

he said. “Sit down.”

The boy took out a book from his bag and then laid it on the table.


And the man talked… to the boy.

It wasn't small talk.

It was teaching.

Careful explanations. Patient corrections. Encouragement.

At one moment, the boy wrinkled his nose at his book.

I don't understand this part,\

There was no frustration in his voice. No impatience.

Just calm.


A day later, two boys.

Then three.

A week later, Table Seven was not a table.

It was now a classroom.

Some students came at different times. Some stayed longer. Some left early. But they all came for the same reason.

To learn.


Ada eventually was overcome by curiosity.

One day as he was preparing to leave, she called out to him.

“Excuse me” she said.

He turned.

“Yes?”

She hesitated for a second.

“I have seen you here a couple of times…I was just wondering…”

She was struggling with the words.

He waited patiently.

\

she asked. “Why not teach somewhere else?”

He looked around the café.

“Because I was found here,” he replied.

Ada frowned slightly. “What do you mean?”

He began to play with the strap of his backpack.

“I used to work at a school, as a teacher,” he said. Until I got sacked.”

There was no malice in his voice. It was simply a matter of fact.

“For a while I wondered what to do. Then one of my students happened to see me here. We talked. He asked for my help in his studies.

He smiled slightly.

“So I helped him.”

Ada looked at the table behind him.

“And the others?”

\

he said.


Ada was in her corner that evening, but it was different.

She remembered the whispers.

The assumptions.

The inferences they made.

All from what they saw… or thought they saw.

An out-of-place-looking man.

A man who drank tea.

A man who sat at Table Seven.


But they didn't see the whole man.

They didn't see the teacher.

They didn't see the patience.

They didn't see the difference.


And so it dawned on her.

When we don't see anything from the outside…

…sometimes look closer.

When the man came back the next day Ada looked him in the eye.

She smiled at him.

And he smiled at her.

…truthfully all you need to know someone…

…is a little time to find out who they are.

body.title: Trusted with Feathers: How Caring for My Neighbor’s Chickens Became a Lifeline
body.body:
![collage.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/leighdalisay/AKGbgq9enLX7paXgfXJ5T8WdLFasBv3EueT9CHZZtVwQE7e5fGsmWjBY7zoyT6n.jpeg)

**Hello Hive Fam! Greetings to all the wonderful pet lovers across the world, especially those in the Hive Pets Community!** It’s always uplifting to share stories with people who understand the joy and responsibility of caring for animals. Today, I’d like to give you a little update about one of my side hustles that I’ve mentioned before.

![2eb1e5b4-462b-44cc-beba-ea740faafded.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/leighdalisay/EoeEpuW3Dmb5echKEZQgHyCz3DXkiSZt3PJuJ7o4nNvitdx9qsygxeVmesPaycUGV5f.jpeg)

![e8879d2b-13e9-4a45-87ae-b445bddc2829.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/leighdalisay/Eoc82Si5KnJ6YxoBLCymmNZuhCZfCna8zMcKtJ8z58D91R5EA3PfyGdqALo7oVvowr8.jpeg)

As I shared previously, my neighbor entrusted me with the feeding of his chickens. Back then, there were only three, but now the flock has grown to six! I’m currently looking after 2 female chickens, 2 male chickens, and 2 baby chicks. Every day, I make sure they get their food and water around 5:00 to 5:30 pm.

![40378546-c67d-48cb-b37d-1668f6ba29d6.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/leighdalisay/EoCiCR1Dzzqk3VrqbbJ6ucv68BRkyhG9cpMfqQ9TWEY8gcEsK9W76bFeSw22Uuyopmp.jpeg)

Even though they aren’t technically mine, I treat them as if they were. My neighbor placed his trust in me, and I take that responsibility seriously. He and his wife are nearing their senior citizen years, and since they also have chickens in their backyard, it can be tiring for them to manage everything. That’s where I step in.

![a3579098-2220-4564-b464-288c5d74b7d1.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/leighdalisay/EoeFSieEPrJZUx32SYqvec5iAfNB7peDWZV2WpcepUAe7ECj3kCbkHN4VdhLWBwN6v5.jpeg)

While I earn a little from this task, it’s more than just income; it’s a big help to me as the sole breadwinner of my family. With mountains of loans and bills to deal with, every bit of support counts. This side hustle has become both meaningful and practical, reminding me that even small opportunities can make a big difference.

body.title: Beautiful day, finally got my prosthesis, walk around town, a simple dinner and TV series!/ ¡Un día precioso! Por fin tengo mi prótesis. Paseo por la ciudad, cena sencilla y serie de televisión.
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR4UWwLv8Vofunb9UPi4imRpx9DjyYLqTR2E6Tqsu9Qkh/1777055249562.jpg)

Good evening blog friends, how are you? Today was another beautiful day, with beautiful sunshine and quite productive, in the meantime today I finished my journey at the dentist, after almost a year of dental work, pain, money and appointments I finally received my removable denture because unfortunately I am missing some lower teeth at the bottom and so I had to put in a removable denture made of metal and with resin teeth, I could have put in fixed implants but the costs would have been really very high and even the idea of having my mouth open again didn't inspire me much, I have already suffered too much for these teeth, now I have my new denture with a denture holder and dedicated toothbrush, for now it is quite annoying, it is strange to have a foreign body in my mouth and I struggle to speak, smoke and let alone eat, in fact to eat I had to take it off but I have to get used to wearing it as often as possible so that it becomes natural to me, the dentist says it will take several weeks unfortunately and it is also possible that I will have to go back for a visit to adjust the denture if I feel it is too loose or too tight or if it hurts, we will see I have my check-up in two weeks.

> Buenas noches, amigos del blog, ¿cómo están? Hoy fue otro hermoso día, con un hermoso sol y bastante productivo. Mientras tanto, hoy terminé mi viaje al dentista. Después de casi un año de trabajo dental, dolor, dinero y citas, finalmente recibí mi dentadura removible porque, desafortunadamente, me faltan algunos dientes inferiores en la parte de abajo y por eso tuve que colocar una dentadura removible hecha de metal y con dientes de resina. Podría haberme puesto implantes fijos, pero los costos habrían sido realmente muy altos e incluso la idea de tener mi boca abierta de nuevo no me inspiraba mucho. Ya he sufrido demasiado por estos dientes. Ahora tengo mi nueva dentadura con un soporte para dentadura y un cepillo de dientes dedicado. Por ahora es bastante molesto, es extraño tener un cuerpo extraño en mi boca y me cuesta hablar, fumar y mucho menos comer. De hecho, para comer tuve que quitármela, pero tengo que acostumbrarme a usarla lo más a menudo posible para que se vuelva natural para mí. El dentista dice que lamentablemente tomará varias semanas y también es posible que tenga que volver para una visita para ajustar la dentadura si siento que está demasiado suelta o demasiado apretada o si Me duele, ya veremos. Tengo mi revisión en dos semanas.

The good thing is that since the weather was nice, I also took advantage of it to take a tour of the city. Pistoia, which is no longer my hometown but the closest one to me, is still a city I love and never tire of exploring. In fact, I always try to walk down new streets and find new places in the city. Today I walked down one of the downtown streets that run alongside the square where my dentist is located. This side of the city is also lined with the typical colorful houses of the area, and I photographed some details I liked about this walk. When I got home, I confess, I didn't feel like cooking much, so I made myself a quick chicken steak. This dish is easy to make because it cooks in just a few minutes and pairs well with any side dish, including a simple salad. Now I'm relaxing on the couch watching a series on Disney Plus called Candy, a thriller based on a true story that I'm really enjoying, starring the brilliant Jessica Biel. Now, goodbye, see you tomorrow, blog friends!
Lo bueno es que, como hacía buen tiempo, aproveché para recorrer la ciudad. Pistoia, que ya no es mi ciudad natal pero sí la más cercana, sigue siendo una ciudad que me encanta y que nunca me canso de explorar. De hecho, siempre intento caminar por calles nuevas y descubrir nuevos rincones. Hoy caminé por una de las calles del centro que bordea la plaza donde está mi dentista. Esta zona de la ciudad también está llena de las típicas casas coloridas de la región, y fotografié algunos detalles que me gustaron del paseo. Al llegar a casa, confieso que no tenía muchas ganas de cocinar, así que me preparé un filete de pollo rápido. Este plato es fácil de hacer porque se cocina en pocos minutos y combina bien con cualquier guarnición, incluso con una ensalada sencilla. Ahora estoy relajándome en el sofá viendo una serie en Disney Plus llamada Candy, un thriller basado en una historia real que me está gustando mucho, protagonizado por la brillante Jessica Biel. ¡Hasta mañana, amigos del blog!

body.title: Home ownership isn't out of reach
body.body:
##  Homeownership and the American Dream 
Are often described as unaffordable today. I keep seeing people claim that renting is more affordable than owning, and that idea simply doesn’t hold up, yet it’s surprising how many people believe it. The truth is, buying a home has always been expensive, no matter the decade. If you compare what people earned in the 1920s to what homes cost, it was just as stressful, if not more so, to come up with a down payment and qualify for a loan.
In fact, back then programs like FHA didn’t even exist. The Federal Housing Administration was created during the Great Depression to make homeownership more accessible, especially for those with lower incomes. FHA doesn’t lend money directly, it insures loans made by approved lenders, reducing their risk and allowing buyers to put less money down. While a 20 percent down payment is ideal, FHA loans typically require around 3.5 percent, and there are programs available to help with that. USDA loans can require even less, sometimes offering zero down options.
## The Numbers 
When you look at the numbers, the barrier to entry isn’t as high as many think. On a $100,000 home, a 3.5 percent down payment is $3,500, which is often comparable to what people spend on deposits and moving costs for a rental. In many cases, that amount is similar to a tax refund. A mortgage on a $100,000 home, including taxes and insurance, might be around $700 per month, give or take depending on credit and down payment.
## Spending habits
So why aren’t more people buying homes? There are three main reasons.
First, spending habits. In the past, people had fewer costly entertainment options. They spent time at home, with family, music, games, and community gatherings that cost little or nothing. People packed lunches, cooked meals, drank water, and avoided unnecessary daily expenses like expensive coffee or frequent dining out. They prioritized saving over spending on nonessential items.
Second, a lack of credit education. Many people don’t fully understand how credit works or how to use it effectively. There are two main types of credit, long term credit such as mortgages, car loans, and student loans, and revolving credit like credit cards. While all loans require on time payments, revolving credit requires careful management. High interest short term loans and cash advances can be avoided entirely if credit cards are used correctly.
## Building good credit
The key is to start with no annual fee cards that offer cash back. If your credit is low or nonexistent, a secured credit card is a good starting point. You deposit an amount equal to your limit, for example $300, and use the card responsibly. Keep your balance low, around 10 percent or less of your limit, and pay it off in full each billing cycle. This avoids interest and earns rewards. The most important rule is to only use the card for purchases you already have the money to cover, essentially treating it like a debit card.
## False Beliefs
Third, the belief that renting is cheaper than owning. Many people argue that maintenance and repairs make home-ownership more expensive, but when you rent, you are covering your landlord’s mortgage, insurance, taxes, maintenance, and profit, while they gain the equity. As of early 2026, average rent in the U.S. ranges roughly from $1,740 to $2,000 per month for about 900 square feet, with costs varying widely by location. Meanwhile, a modest home with a $700 mortgage creates a potential monthly difference of $250 to $750.
If someone saved even half of that difference for maintenance and invested the rest, they would be building equity, growing their net worth, and reducing financial stress over time.
## But you don't understand Argument 
I understand these challenges personally. I used to struggle with spending and credit, and it took time to figure out how to change. Eventually, I realized I didn’t need to spend money to enjoy life or maintain strong relationships. I started saving, using coupons, and being intentional with spending. Over time, that led to purchasing land, which we used as a down payment on a construction-to-FHA loan. We built a smaller home for under $100,000, and within a few years its value more than doubled.
That didn’t happen overnight, and it didn’t happen by accident. It came from changing how we thought about money, improving our habits, and choosing to invest in our future.

body.title: [ENG/ESP]  Ugliest Animal Challenge - Crocodile (Crocodylus acutus) AN / Desafío Animal más feo - Cocodrilo (Crocodylus acutus) AN
body.body:
**The Minas Crocodile Farm**

The sun was beginning to warm the Camagüey countryside when our small team of researchers—biologists Elena Morales, Carlos Fuentes, and myself—traveled the last few kilometers of red earth separating the central highway from the Minas Crocodile Farm. We had spent weeks preparing for this visit, eager to see firsthand the center that, since 1985, has become a beacon for the conservation of these fascinating creatures in Cuba. A day of observation, interviews, and learning about one of the most emblematic reptiles of the Cuban archipelago awaited us.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYXQYq8bsPYEnpF6LofiN13Zk4uURiGqsSY7AsTZDXM9x/1777045363690.jpg)



Upon our arrival, we were received by the experienced breeder Juan Luis Núñez, who would be our guide throughout the journey.

**Visit to the farm**

The farm extends over approximately nine caballerías—more than 120 hectares—bathed by the mighty waters of the Máximo River, which snakes alongside the facilities and gives them an almost unreal greenery.

Currently, the facility houses more than 1,500 specimens of Crocodylus acutus, the American crocodile, and work is underway on the construction of four new lagoons with the goal of exceeding five thousand specimens in the near future. Juan Luis Núñez clarified that, although this species is not native to Cuba, it arrived a long time ago and has adapted perfectly to the conditions of the Caribbean.

The human team behind this noble environmental effort is made up of five women and 34 men, who diligently care for every detail of the reproductive process. In the different ponds, we were able to observe everything from the youngest hatchlings to imposing adults resting semi-submerged, with only their eyes and nostrils protruding from the surface.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZNkUo8X5Bg6jf5N7zZK9G9w7quLoKDMwZaYpjkyXzdJY/1777045869257.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTq6ssWR9xgQLhijT4Nu629oJyaaPJ2Xe2pF1qSKwMy8f/1777045963768.jpg)

**General characteristics and taxonomy**

Back at the farm's office, Yosvany González Fernández, a veterinarian in charge of caring for the Crocodylus acutus family, gave us a detailed talk about the characteristics of Cuban crocodiles.

Cuba is home to two native species of crocodiles. The first is the Cuban crocodile (Crocodylus rhombifer), a species endemic to the archipelago found in the Ciénaga de Lanier on the Isle of Youth (where it is rare to find it today) and in the Ciénaga de Zapata in Matanzas. This reptile prefers the fresh waters of estuaries, lagoons, and canals, although it has also been observed in coastal areas.

The second is the American crocodile (Crocodylus acutus), which has a much wider distribution and is found in 11 of Cuba's 14 provinces, as well as on the Isle of Youth and numerous keys. This species prefers the brackish waters of coastal lagoons, estuaries, and river mouths.

Regarding physical characteristics, both share the typical traits of crocodilians: a wide, flattened, triangular-shaped head, strong jaws with very sharp teeth, ear openings on both sides of the head, and prominent eyes and nostrils that allow them to see and breathe while keeping their bodies submerged.

However, Yosvany pointed out the key differences between the two species: the American crocodile has a more elongated jaw, an average of 68 teeth, green eyes, and is generally less aggressive than the Cuban. Meanwhile, the Cuban crocodile has longer than usual legs, a shorter and broader snout, and wider, brighter scales (yellow and black). The bright colors of the Cuban crocodile are one of its most attention-grabbing features.

A fascinating piece of information Yosvany revealed to us: the sex of these animals depends on the incubation temperature. If the temperature is below 30 degrees Celsius, the hatchling is male; if it is higher, the crocodile will be female. The optimal temperature during incubation must be maintained between 28 and 34 degrees.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW4mw85zZu5p7oA3q87nfcpa42f54fapRpHXozTCrJEhR/1777055667529.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUffEcScHahztw49gAzgobDXU27gdbcJsrjAyLojZSTf1/1777055552668.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdfizkK3J4bdAaB4cXVBZXPcmPrvURMxPt37N7E8U3WzC/1777055498755.jpg)


**Diet and hunting habits**

At lunchtime, we took the opportunity to talk with the workers in charge of feeding. They explained that the crocodiles' diet varies considerably depending on their age and size. When they are small, they feed on insects, crustaceans, mollusks, frogs, and small fish, increasing the size of their prey as they grow.

In the case of the American crocodile, stomach content studies have revealed a surprisingly varied diet that includes fish such as the patao (Eugerres plumieri), the mojarra (Gerres cinereus), and the biajaca (Ciclosoma tetracanta); crustaceans such as land crabs (Cardiosoma guanhumi), blue crabs (Callinectes sp.), and shrimp (Penaeus sp.); reptiles such as the mangrove water snake (Natrix sipedon) and the Cuban slider (Pseudemys decussata); as well as birds such as the double-crested cormorant (Phalacrocorax auritus), the American flamingo (Phoenicopterus ruber), and the anhinga (Anhinga anhinga).

The Cuban crocodile, for its part, includes fish, frogs, turtles, snakes, birds, and small mammals in its diet. One of the most surprising abilities of this species is its capacity to launch itself vertically out of the water, practically standing on its tail to catch animals in trees. Each specimen must receive between 3 and 7 percent of its body weight in food.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYRnMiKtJkdRuHD4jVnajaUyPNoyY95TtRiKxfnYtNX93/1777055766682.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdGck8d6e4n9hU8RCuRw4Kjj4C4yPCqqdRxTQVyDXA7vC/1777055729927.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd5HvVxvGd5S3EjpBwdqbYXyuotzhzzWSmFCDvXBFoHwj/1777055406934.jpg)



**Ecological importance and role in the food chain**

In the afternoon, we met with the center's biologists to discuss the ecological role of these reptiles. The conversation was revealing: within the swamp ecosystem, crocodiles are the main predators and ecosystem engineers, playing a key role in maintaining the structure and function of the environment.

These reptiles perform fundamental ecological functions such as selective predation on fish species, nutrient recycling, and the maintenance of water refuges during droughts. They act as sentinels of the health of the Ciénaga de Zapata, the largest wetland and protected area in the Caribbean, where humans, animals, and the environment are all so deeply connected.

Carlos Fuentes, our marine biologist, explained that the Cuban crocodile is considered to have the smallest geographic range of all crocodiles in the world. This situation, along with factors such as illegal hunting, climate change, and hybridization with the American crocodile, severely impacts its survival and has led it to be classified by the IUCN as \

Hybridization between the two species is a particularly serious problem, as the resulting offspring are fertile and can cause genetic contamination that threatens the purity of both bloodlines. This phenomenon occurs both in natural populations and in captivity.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVsxRC8DygbsuZn1X3XDUhKPkN8WUhiYvVncRLXgYqhqS/1777055287939.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYRnMiKtJkdRuHD4jVnajaUyPNoyY95TtRiKxfnYtNX93/1777054474875.jpg)

**Other important elements**

Juan Luis Núñez explained to us that, in their natural habitat, hatchling survival barely reaches between two and five percent due to human action (hunting for commercial purposes), cannibalism, and other predators. Thanks to the dedication of the farm's workers, hatching success rates in captivity reach between 45 and 60 percent.

Crocodile skin has also historically been highly valued for making shoes, handbags, rugs, and other artisanal objects, which has encouraged illegal hunting.

**A final comment**

As we said goodbye to the farm, we carried with us not only data and photographs, but also a deep understanding of the importance of these animals for Cuba's ecological balance. Crocodiles, those prehistoric beings that have survived for more than 70 million years, now face their greatest challenge: survival in a world transformed by humanity.

In places like the Minas Crocodile Farm, hope is renewed. With more than 1,500 protected specimens and an ambitious expansion plan, this Camagüey center stands as a bastion in the conservation of these fascinating creatures. As Yosvany told us before we left: \

I invite my friends @estelacha, @frannyon, @nony and @theinfiltred to participate.

*Note: The photos are my own.
I used the DeepL Translate translator*.





**ESPAÑOL** 



El sol comenzaba a calentar la campiña camagüeyana cuando nuestro pequeño equipo de investigadores —los biólogos Elena Morales, Carlos Fuentes y quien esto escribe— atravesamos los últimos kilómetros de tierra roja que separaban la carretera central del Criadero de Cocodrilos de Minas. Llevábamos semanas preparando esta visita, ansiosos por conocer de primera mano el centro que desde 1985 se ha convertido en un faro de conservación de estas fascinantes criaturas en Cuba. Nos esperaba una jornada de observación, entrevistas y aprendizaje sobre uno de los reptiles más emblemáticos del archipiélago cubano.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYXQYq8bsPYEnpF6LofiN13Zk4uURiGqsSY7AsTZDXM9x/1777045363690.jpg)


A nuestra llegada, fuimos recibidos por el experimentado criador Juan Luis Núñez, quien sería nuestro guía durante la travesía.  

 **Visita al criadero**

El criadero se extiende sobre un terreno de aproximadamente nueve caballerías —más de 120 hectáreas— bañado por las portentosas aguas del río Máximo, que serpentea junto a las instalaciones y las dota de un verdor casi irreal.  

Actualmente, la instalación alberga más de 1500 ejemplares de Crocodylus acutus, el cocodrilo americano, y se trabaja en la construcción de cuatro nuevas lagunas con el objetivo de superar los cinco mil especímenes en un futuro cercano. Juan Luis Núñez nos aclaró que, aunque esta especie no es oriunda de Cuba, llegó hace mucho tiempo y se ha adaptado perfectamente a las condiciones del Caribe.

El equipo humano detrás de esta noble gestión medioambiental está compuesto por cinco mujeres y 34 hombres, quienes con esmero cuidan cada detalle del proceso reproductivo. En los diferentes estanques, pudimos observar desde las más tiernas crías hasta imponentes adultos que reposaban semisumergidos, con los ojos y orificios nasales apenas sobresaliendo de la superficie.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZNkUo8X5Bg6jf5N7zZK9G9w7quLoKDMwZaYpjkyXzdJY/1777045869257.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTq6ssWR9xgQLhijT4Nu629oJyaaPJ2Xe2pF1qSKwMy8f/1777045963768.jpg)


 **Características generales y taxonomía**

De regreso en la oficina del criadero, Yosvany González Fernández, médico veterinario encargado del cuidado de la familia Crocodylus acutus, nos ofreció una detallada charla sobre las características de los cocodrilos cubanos.

Cuba es hogar de dos especies nativas de cocodrilos. La primera es el cocodrilo cubano (Crocodylus rhombifer), una especie endémica del archipiélago que se localiza en la Ciénaga de Lanier, en Isla de la Juventud (donde es raro encontrarlo hoy en día), y en la Ciénaga de Zapata, en Matanzas. Este reptil prefiere las aguas dulces de esteros, lagunas y canales, aunque también se ha observado en zonas costeras.

El segundo es el cocodrilo americano (Crocodylus acutus), que tiene una distribución mucho más amplia y se encuentra en 11 de las 14 provincias cubanas, además de Isla de la Juventud y numerosos cayos. Esta especie prefiere las aguas salobres de lagunas costeras, esteros y desembocaduras de ríos.

En cuanto a las características físicas, ambos comparten los rasgos típicos de los crocodílidos: cabeza ancha y aplanada de forma triangular, fuertes mandíbulas con dientes muy afilados, aberturas de oídos a ambos lados de la cabeza, y ojos y orificios nasales prominentes que les permiten ver y respirar mientras mantienen el cuerpo sumergido.

Sin embargo, Yosvany nos señaló las diferencias clave entre ambas especies: el cocodrilo americano presenta una mandíbula más alargada, un promedio de 68 dientes, el color verde de sus ojos y, generalmente, son menos agresivos que los cubanos. Por su parte, el cocodrilo cubano tiene las patas más largas de lo habitual, la cara más corta y ancha, y escamas más amplias y de colores más brillantes (amarillo y negro). Los colores brillantes del cocodrilo cubano son una de las características que más atención atraen.


Una curiosidad fascinante que nos reveló Yosvany: el sexo de estos animales depende de la temperatura de incubación. Si la temperatura es inferior a los 30 grados Celsius, la cría sale macho; si es superior, el cocodrilo será hembra. La temperatura óptima durante la incubación debe mantenerse entre los 28 y 34 grados.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW4mw85zZu5p7oA3q87nfcpa42f54fapRpHXozTCrJEhR/1777055667529.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUffEcScHahztw49gAzgobDXU27gdbcJsrjAyLojZSTf1/1777055552668.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdfizkK3J4bdAaB4cXVBZXPcmPrvURMxPt37N7E8U3WzC/1777055498755.jpg)


**Alimentación y hábitos de caza**

A la hora del almuerzo, aprovechamos para conversar con los trabajadores encargados de la alimentación. Nos explicaron que la dieta de los cocodrilos varía considerablemente según su edad y tamaño. Cuando son pequeños, se alimentan de insectos, crustáceos, moluscos, ranas y peces pequeños, aumentando el tamaño de la presa a medida que van creciendo.

En el caso del cocodrilo americano, los estudios de contenido estomacal han revelado una dieta sorprendentemente variada que incluye peces como el patao (Eugerres plumieri), la mojarra (Gerres cinereus) y la biajaca (Ciclosoma tetracanta); crustáceos como cangrejos de tierra (Cardiosoma guanhumi), jaibas (Callinectes sp.) y camarones (Penaeus sp.); reptiles como el cativo de mangle (Natrix sipedon) y las jicoteas (Pseudemys decussata); así como aves como la corúa de mar (Phalacrocorax auritus), el flamenco (Phoenicopterus ruber) y la marbella (Anhinga anhinga).

El cocodrilo cubano, por su parte, incluye en su alimentación peces, ranas, tortugas, serpientes, aves y pequeños mamíferos. Una de las habilidades más sorprendentes de esta especie es su capacidad para salir del agua verticalmente, parándose prácticamente sobre la cola para atrapar animales en los árboles. Cada ejemplar debe recibir entre el 3 y el 7 por ciento de su peso corporal en alimento.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYRnMiKtJkdRuHD4jVnajaUyPNoyY95TtRiKxfnYtNX93/1777055766682.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdGck8d6e4n9hU8RCuRw4Kjj4C4yPCqqdRxTQVyDXA7vC/1777055729927.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd5HvVxvGd5S3EjpBwdqbYXyuotzhzzWSmFCDvXBFoHwj/1777055406934.jpg)


**Importancia ecológica y papel en la cadena alimenticia**

Por la tarde, nos reunimos con los biólogos del centro para discutir el papel ecológico de estos reptiles. La conversación fue reveladora: dentro del ecosistema de los pantanos, los cocodrilos son los principales depredadores e ingenieros del ecosistema, y desempeñan un papel clave en el mantenimiento de la estructura y función del medio ambiente.

Estos reptiles realizan funciones ecológicas fundamentales como la depredación selectiva de especies de peces, el reciclaje de nutrientes y el mantenimiento de refugios con agua durante las sequías. Actúan como centinelas de la salud de la Ciénaga de Zapata, el mayor humedal y área protegida del Caribe, donde los humanos, los animales y el medio ambiente están todos tan conectados.

Carlos Fuentes, nuestro biólogo marino, nos explicó que el cocodrilo cubano es considerado el de menor rango de distribución geográfica entre todos los cocodrilos del mundo. Esta situación, junto a factores como la caza ilegal, el cambio climático y la hibridación con el cocodrilo americano, impactan gravemente en su supervivencia y lo han llevado a ser clasificado por la UICN como \

.

La hibridación entre ambas especies es un problema particularmente grave, ya que la progenie resultante es fértil y puede causar una contaminación genética que amenaza la pureza de ambas líneas sanguíneas. Este fenómeno ocurre tanto en poblaciones naturales como en cautiverio.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVsxRC8DygbsuZn1X3XDUhKPkN8WUhiYvVncRLXgYqhqS/1777055287939.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYRnMiKtJkdRuHD4jVnajaUyPNoyY95TtRiKxfnYtNX93/1777054474875.jpg)

 
**Otros elementos importantes**

Juan Luis Núñez nos explicó que, en su hábitat natural, la supervivencia de las crías apenas alcanza entre un dos y un cinco por ciento debido a la acción del hombre que los caza para fines comerciales, el canibalismo y otros depredadores. Gracias al esmero de los trabajadores del criadero, se alcanza en cautiverio entre el 45 y el 60 por ciento de efectividad en los nacimientos.

La piel de cocodrilo también ha sido históricamente muy valorada para la confección de zapatos, carteras, alfombras y otros objetos artesanales, lo que ha incentivado la caza ilegal. 

 

**Un comentario final** 

Al despedirnos del criadero, llevábamos con nosotros no solo datos y fotografías, sino una profunda comprensión de la importancia de estos animales para el equilibrio ecológico de Cuba. Los cocodrilos, esos seres prehistóricos que han sobrevivido durante más de 70 millones de años, se enfrentan hoy a su mayor desafío: la supervivencia en un mundo transformado por el hombre.

En lugares como el Criadero de Minas, la esperanza se renueva. Con más de 1500 ejemplares protegidos y un ambicioso plan de expansión, este centro camagüeyano se erige como un baluarte en la conservación de estas fascinantes criaturas. Como nos dijo Yosvany antes de partir: \

.

Invito a participar a mis amigos @estelacha, @frannyon, @nony y @theinfiltred.

*Nota: Las fotos son de mías.
Utilicé el traductor DeepL Translate*.

body.title: Daredevil Born Again: Gloves Off – S02E04 - RECAP
body.body:
https://i.postimg.cc/wvLHVF1c/Dare-Devil-Born-Again-(2025)-S02E05-RECAP-000.gif

[Source](https://www.disneyplus.com/browse/entity-85e7a914-c8e6-41db-95df-c740dc2cf1b7)

https://i.imgur.com/PGNq5Ek.png

Today decided to stay home, was not really feeling that well, mostly the cold. I decided to double down and catch up on my Daredevil posts after not doing much, I had a draft for both so was easier and less effort, right now Daredevil Born Again is my favorite show even though Im also watching MONARCH, episode 5 titled The Grand Design did not disappoint me at all. The episode opens with something completely new for what this season has been doing, because instead of throwing more action at you it pulls things back and decides to breathe, using this really clever aspect ratio shift that transports you visually into the Netflix era of the show, the colors go warmer, and suddenly you feel like you are watching Daredevil 2015 all over again, and it is such a dope move that I never though they would do but makes more sense with the mood of the series at this point. Foggy Nelson back in the screen was a cool touch, not necesarly because he is one of my favorite characters of the story but mainly because you forget how much that dude grounded Matt Murdock until he is standing there again in that old law office looking young and arguing about mercy for some lowlife nobody they were assign to defend when the dude clearly knows his future but Foggy know the guy and think if he had better options in life he might just be different, and it reframes the whole Matt and Foggy relationship without feeling like a cheap nostalgia grab for online aura farming. The flashback structure is really good with Matt and Foggy taking a case defending Leo McCoy, a guy who used to bully Foggy as a kid, someone who treated him like shit till the day, is the moral engine that keeps everything going for Matt in the present, it is that connection between past grace and present choice that makes the hour feel patient and earned rather than just a filler episode and the show does not try to rush that connection either, it just lets it build across the whole episode.

- IMDB: https://www.imdb.com/title/tt18923754/
- Platform: [{{PLATFORM}}](https://www.disneyplus.com/browse/entity-85e7a914-c8e6-41db-95df-c740dc2cf1b7)

https://bo.skiptvads.blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-9-1776288292-overlay.png
<div style=\

> https://t6.picb.cc/2026/04/24/uFEPFu.png [Source](https://www.disneyplus.com/browse/entity-85e7a914-c8e6-41db-95df-c740dc2cf1b7) The Wilson Fisk side of this episode is tragic and I mean that because even when is the villain men that was a hard hit he got, because the visual work they do around Vanessa is some of the most thoughtful stuff this show has ever attempted, it really shows how much they love each other. The episode uses Vanessa seeing the Rabbit in a Snowstorm painting, that same painting from the very first season of the Netflix show that brought Wilson and Vanessa together at the art gallery and it runs parallel to the flashback that shows Vanessa before she ever met Fisk, back when she was just a woman working at a gallery trying to convince her boss to hang an all white painting that nobody wanted to show. Watching Wilson in the present it all what is happening to Vanessa while the story simultaneously shows you the exact moment their love story began is a very well thought piece of storytelling, the kind of mirror like situation you expect from something like very dramatic romance show but almost never get from a Marvel and D Onofrio does not even have to say much because his face is doing ninety percent of the work. His body language in the Vanessa scenes this episode is just quietly devastating, the way he pauses before answering people, they guy is really broke down, it is the kind of performance where you can feel the character processing grief in real time without the show having to spell it out. The episode also brings back James Wesley through the flashback, with Toby Leonard Moore showing up to remind you how tight that machine around Fisk once was and the way Wesley connects to both the McCoy case and the Fisk Vanessa meeting is clever writing that ties the past to the present without feeling forced. https://t6.picb.cc/2026/04/24/uFExJD.png [Source](https://www.disneyplus.com/browse/entity-85e7a914-c8e6-41db-95df-c740dc2cf1b7) https://t6.picb.cc/2026/04/24/uFET4v.png [Source](https://www.disneyplus.com/browse/entity-85e7a914-c8e6-41db-95df-c740dc2cf1b7) There were moments in the episode I wanted more of but the show simply does not go there, one clear example is how Karen Page shows up at the end of the episode and has zero lines, she is basically just there when Matt brings Bullseye to the hideout and the episode closes on her face seeing what Matt has done, I was expecting her to flip out on Matt for him showing mercy to the guy he wanted to kill so desperatly, its that Foggy soul in him, this sets up an obvious future conflict between them but does not actually develop it in this episode at all. That story is coming for sure, you can feel it in the setup, but it is not played out here and I respect the show for taking its time with it rather than cramming it in. What the episode gives you instead is the Matt and Bullseye back and forward, Matt trying to save him and Dex wanting to die for everything he has done to Matt, he insist its just and equation, all this argument while on the run through the city, which is fascinating because Matt is dragging this injured psychopath through underground tunnels to a church, feeling responsible for keeping him alive, and Bullseye is sitting there bleeding out and telling Matt to just leave him to die, the conversations they have about whether people can change and whether mercy even makes sense for someone like Bullseye is the real philosophical meat of the whole hour. There is one moment where Matt chokes Bullseye after he mentions Foggy by name and you see exactly how much grief Matt is still carrying under all that catholic guilt and morals of his, it is a small thing but those small things are what this episode keeps nailing. https://t6.picb.cc/2026/04/24/uFE9ji.png [Source](https://www.disneyplus.com/browse/entity-85e7a914-c8e6-41db-95df-c740dc2cf1b7) https://t6.picb.cc/2026/04/24/uFELKL.png [Source](https://www.disneyplus.com/browse/entity-85e7a914-c8e6-41db-95df-c740dc2cf1b7) What this episode does better than most of this season is use its flashbacks to actually say something about the present rather than just being nostalgia service, I know there were moments that it felt the episode was giving Vanessa too much screen time but I think they were just trying to exploit Fisk suffering, and that is a harder needle to thread than it looks, I am thinking about shows that have tried this and ended up feeling like they were overextending their story instead of building something. The flashbacks to Matt and Foggy arguing the McCoy case, the guy Wesley was trying to have killed inside the prison system while they were defending him on the outside, those moments running in parallel because it shows you the same corrupt system use to operate back then is nothing new to what he is applying during his run in NY as the mayor, it has always been there, grinding people up quietly while the courts pretend to work. The pacing jumps around going from the warm orange tones of the past to the cold blue of Matt moving Bullseye through the city and the visual contrast between those two timelines did some real work for the story rather than just being a style choice. The debate this episode is really wrestling with is mercy and legal duty, whether Foggy defending his childhood bully as a kid set a moral standard that Matt is now forced to honor even when the person in front of him is Foggy's killer and that is a way more interesting argument than any big fight scene could have delivered. The best part of this implementation during the episode is that the episode does not try to resolve it neatly because it does not have a clean answer to what is more important if mercy or moral. https://i.imgur.com/uwwnjtd.png

> https://i.imgur.com/r0yj9oi.png I am giving this episode a 8 out of 10 and I do not feel bad about it at all because this is the kind of hour that reminds you why tv series can still do things movies cannot pull off possibly because there is way more time to pussh and hold the throttle, it gives you space to sit with characters and let their choices accumulate over time. Wilson Fisk is losing his grip on everything he built because the violence he used to control the world has now consumed the one person who made him human instead of the monster that he is, and watching D Onofrio carry that grief while the show throws back to the moment Vanessa first walked into his life is sad and that on top of Fisk suffering is just pure good drama. Matt is on the run through Hell Kitchen keeping a murderer alive out of some sense of righteousness that even he cannot fully explain, and Foggy is there in the past reminding him what it means to believe the system can work even when it obviously is not. I go back to when Karen watch both arrive its just mind blowing how she would feel, for comparison like when Matt lost it for a second when Dex mention Foggy, you can feel that whole confrontation building from a mile away between Karen and Matt, its not going to be easy to settle and I think things are going to flip now where Matt choose to be merciful DareDevil and its Karen who seek revenge at all cost. This episode is proof that Born Again Season 2 is not coasting on nostalgia and action sequences, it is actually trying to say something real about these people underneath the masks and the violence. https://i.imgur.com/uwwnjtd.png https://i.imgur.com/AbuDA6i.png

body.title: Change Is Real,But Do We Allow It?
body.body: > Growth as we all know by now is a part of human nature. Who you were years ago isn’t who you are today. You’re an entirely different person now- your thinking, how you view things, how you move and how you interact with others. It’s one of two thing though- it’s either you have become a better person or your habits have deteriorated to become very bad. Either way, I would say change is change. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeTamCmMKsXDwAGoRBGGJrkQK9e3UZgM1Ud5goYT9NBfM/0af4d383_1774_437b_82e6_a5520221c479.jpeg) As you probably know by now, as individuals we all go through the growth process whether we like it or not. At some point in our lives, we are okay with anything and everything but we all somehow get to that point where those things are no more enough for us. That’s the point where we start to think deeply about our lives, what we really want, what we don’t want and the changes we want to make in our lives which include the kind of company we keep and everything in between. They say show me your friend and I’ll show you your character and this couldn’t have been said any better because that’s just it. The kind of people you walk with reflect who you are to some extent. I understand it might not be the case for everyone but majority of carries the vote on this one. So, it safe to say that they company you keep to some extent influence your thoughts as well as your actions- if you’re not someone who already knows what their about. And thanks to social media, some of us get so into it we start doing things online which are bound to be used against us in the future. You’d agree with me that everyone sees things from a different perspective. Your thoughts on a topic will be totally different from my thoughts on that same topic which is totally okay. We agree to disagree. What isn’t okay is someone going on to make or pass comments that are totally unacceptable. An example is someone, say a celebrity going on to blame a rape victim even though we all know it’s not their fault. This can lead to a lot of reactions from fans and the general public which can lead to that person being canceled. In that moment, tempers are high and all but if there’s one thing about social media, it’s that the internet never forgets. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfXHrX3msCmzResjSxtSBatJygF4FTVWV51TxtRzeQocp/img_0837.jpg) In a few years time, this issue would probably die down and everyone would move on with his life. Then say out of nowhere this celebrity becomes a victim of harassment or something. There’s a high chance that the people on the internet will use their past comment against him in that situation which shouldn’t be the case. People do change and honestly, our opinion on things change with respect to our experiences. No one should have to bear the weight of their past opinions even after they have a new way of viewing things. As much as we believe it’s the same person, we need to know that physically it’s them but mentally, there’s probably a whole new person in there. It could be me and it could be you. Let’s cut people some slack. Life cannot be without mistakes, give people the benefit of the doubt , allow them grow, allow them learn, unlearn and relearn. Life is all about perspective. - - - all images belong to me. - - - ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXuSJ2V9NneWQW9Jxgobw7BtKvMb3UBPdxv3jaAhx5vpA/f40b32ec_5287_4867_ae7e_9fa77d7f679b.png)

The weather was crisp and clear, perfect for a day of wandering.

As I set off from the picturesque village of Bourton-on-the-Water, known as the \

I was greeted by the iconic low stone bridges arching over the River Windrush. The sound of the water flowing was incredibly soothing, and families were enjoying picnics along the riverbanks. Walking through the lush fields, I spotted sheep grazing peacefully, their woolly coats bright against the green. I also came across a few quaint cottages with thatched roofs, each with their own unique character. The stone walls and honey-colored buildings gave the area a delightful fairy-tale quality. I encountered a local artist painting en plein air, capturing the serene landscape. We struck up a conversation about her inspirations and the beauty of the Cotswolds. She shared stories about how the scenery changes with the seasons, adding a different charm each time. Continuing my walk, I stumbled upon a small farm shop selling homemade jams and freshly baked goods. I couldn’t resist and bought a jar of raspberry jam, which I planned to enjoy later with some scones. As I meandered through the fields, I also met a group of fellow walkers. We exchanged tips on the best routes and discussed our favorite parts of the Cotswolds. It was lovely to connect with others who shared a passion for walking and exploring history. Eventually, I made my way to the historic village of Stow-on-the-Wold, with its antique shops and the impressive market square. I took a moment to sit at a café, sipping tea and reflecting on the day's adventures while watching the world go by. body.body:
**Your core point is right:** marriage gets weaker when it becomes a performance, a legal war plan, or a financial trap instead of a partnership. The image nails that tension well — the bright arch on one side and the wreckage on the other is not subtle, but it works.

Where I’d push back a bit is this: **marriage itself isn’t the problem; bad partner selection and bad expectations are.** The expensive wedding culture is absurd, and the fear around divorce costs is real, but the stronger argument is that too many people prepare for the ceremony and not the actual daily job of living with another human. That’s where trust dies.

On **single parenting**, I agree with you in the broad sense: in an ideal world, stable two-parent homes usually give children more support, time, and resilience. But life is messier than ideals, and a peaceful single-parent home can be far better than a two-parent house full of manipulation, contempt, or chaos. A bad marriage is not morally superior just because it stayed married.

The sharpest part of your post is the link between **economics and commitment**. When basic living costs rise, people don’t just delay marriage because they fear love — they fear bills, housing, and the social expectation that marriage must come with a huge financial display. That part deserves more emphasis than the usual “modern people don’t value family” complaint, because money pressure changes behavior fast.

One note: the line about **women empowerment** needs careful handling. Independence is not the enemy of marriage; **immaturity, selfishness, and lack of accountability** are — and men are just as guilty of that. Strong women don’t destroy marriage. Weak character does.

For community context, the closest related discussion I could point to was thin, so I’d lean on your own framing here rather than pretend there’s a big live debate around it on InLeo right now.

body.title: Marriage or the shackles
body.body:
>

Marriage is known as the social acceptance of a relationship between couples as well as life partners. A marriage is beautiful and heavenly as long as it's between two right people, but finding the right partner is not so easy, and naturally, many times people are entangled with the wrong person, and the relationship becomes toxic. So many of them end up separating. In many countries, men also need to share half of their assets with their wives if separation happens. For such a reason, many don't want to get married. ![Inline Image](https://img.leopedia.io/DQmUhNKALo7o8LSbrUE7MRZSS4F6WZXL9rSqMETmQwd8TSv/ai-image-1777054636786.jpeg) picture generated by rafiki There are also many women who think marriage is one kind of shackle and restricts their freedom. They don't want to restrict themselves, and they want freedom all the time. In recent times, such kinds of thoughts have increased in the minds of many people. Even after having kids, people are interested in single parenting. Is it a good thing? It can be considered good and bad depending on the situation, but from the overall perspective, I don't think that it's something good. Because it shows that the trust between couples is decreasing, and without mature trust, it's very difficult to maintain a healthy relationship. Aside from that reason, most people are afraid of marriage because, at the present time, the economic condition of most countries is not so good, and the prices of all necessary products have increased. Getting married in a traditional way costs a lot. Even in a simple marriage, it costs so much that it may take 1 year to earn that amount of money. So many of them think that getting married is a financial burden, and they are afraid of it and try to avoid marriage. The relationship of a married couple runs on mutual trust and having the mentality to adapt to the situation. Women empowerment is a good thing, but it is also a reason why many women are getting arrogant and don't want to compromise, as they are self-dependent, and their self-pride can also be a reason they don't want to contribute to a relationship. Again, there are issues with men also. Some men also don't like women to be self-dependent, as they think women should be inside the house and take care of the family. It's the old way of thinking, and some men are not ready to adapt to the change as women empowerment is happening. It can also lead to separation. It's a world of equality where both men and women are equal by right. Instead of that, in some cases men need to adapt to the thoughts of their wives, and in some cases, women also need to adapt to the thoughts of their husbands. That's how a relationship can be balanced. Unfortunately, at the present time, both women and men have become arrogant and try to prove themselves better than each other, and because of that, many people are trying to avoid marriage. Humans are not as understanding as they were in the earlier days, and naturally, the trust of people is not as solid as it was in the earlier days, which leads to situations where there is not enough faith in a relationship, and because of that reason many people are not so interested in being bound by marriage.

body.title: 76ers are victorious vs Celtics in Game 2 of First Round of NBA Playoffs and steal homecourt! | Big Game 3 in Philly tonight!
body.body:
![nba-philadelphia-76ers-logo.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/adhammer/AK3eyGpWbyoaTTjJeeKnj44681PrD7tPGkoXMiDJYKDywwjPDVKgyqJH3UhvszU.png)
[Src](https://loodibee.com/nba/nba-philadelphia-76ers-logo/)

VJ Maxx! This nickname for V.J. Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey is growing on me...
![file_000000003f84722f9eeb67724fdc27fd.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/adhammer/EogLumxLPHjNrjsoBk8sHukJF3Jpkhg11qKoQi7nfU63uFsa5eHkjyZiHFBUN3raxhn.png)
Image created with ChatGPT. 

Tuesday's [Game 2 victory](https://youtu.be/gHNogLs7MOk?si=Nx4co4XEcMsVdGF3) was absolutely BRILLIANT! I am so proud of this team. They came into Game 2 with a whole different type of energy. I think any nervousness from Game 1 totally evaporated and they were just ready to play. They moved faster, played more physical, and seemingly stopped overthinking in general. 

It was really electric to watch. I haven't been this excited about a basketball game in awhile. The Sixers started strong, and then the Celtics hit the Sixers with a brutal 16-0 run and I was thinking it was about to be Game 1 all over again...

But the Sixers proved they have a backbone and started to cook. V.J. Edgecombe started the momentum shift in a big way when he scored 16 points in the second quarter alone. By halftime he had 20. 

The Sixers had an eight point lead at halftime and weathered the storm from that point on. Paul George was pretty steady throughout on both sides of the ball.

But Tuesday was mainly about V.J. Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey. After V.J. Edgecombe went off in the second quarter, Tyrese closed the show in the fourth. The Celtics managed to cut the Sixers' lead to two late in the fourth when Tyrese said 'NOPE, not on my watch!'. Tyrese promptly drained two brutal threes to extend the lead back to eight and eventually the Sixers took control once again on their way to a fairly convincing victory. 

CINEMA. PURE CINEMA! I was soooooo hyped!!!!
https://youtu.be/RzoZAO4P-zU?si=YiYW2kUiW38RM8nl
[Src](https://youtu.be/RzoZAO4P-zU?si=YiYW2kUiW38RM8nl)

30 points and 10 rebounds from a 6'4\

power forward. The man is a DAWG!!!! Edgecombe's also officially the [youngest player to drop 30 points and 10 rebounds in a playoff game](https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/breaking-news/article/rookie-vj-edgecombes-playoff-breakout-sends-76ers-past-celtics-puts-him-in-company-with-magic-johnson-013028319.html) in NBA history, surpassing MAGIC JOHNSON.
https://youtu.be/Rxxo3W-9ZkU?si=XQRJgSCHDsnRI2lV
[Src](https://youtu.be/Rxxo3W-9ZkU?si=XQRJgSCHDsnRI2lV)

An unforgettable night no matter what happens the rest of the series!

As fun as Game 2 was, it was one game. Now that I, as a fan, have tasted success I want more! Buuuuut the Celtics are still really good and it's not gonna be easy. They probably won't shoot the ball nearly as poorly as they did in Game 2 and it will be pretty hard for the Sixers to replicate their excellent shooting performance as well. 

The Sixers and Celtics sort of flip flopped in Game 1 and 2 from a shooting perspective. I imagine there will be a return to baseline in Game 3, where both teams shoot at a more average rate I guess. But what do I know, this is the playoffs and these things are hard to predict.

Maybe it's just the optimistic Sixers fan in me but the energy of this series has shifted. The Sixers have belief now and that's going to be hard to shake. Game 1 went predictably well for the Celtics but Game 2 went rather unpredictably well for the **Sixers.** I mean the Sixers won but it really didn't feel like a fluke if that makes sense. The Sixers showed a very interesting level of composure. The Celtics were never fully out of it mathematically, but the Sixers never seemed rattled either. Maybe I'm delusional, time will tell I guess.

Now the Sixers are in Philly for Game 3 and I KNOW the crowd is going to be absolutely tweaking! I AM SO PUMPED!

Apparently Joel Embiid is listed as doubtful too... Now that would be something if he played!

I'm just having fun with it all! Let's goooooooo!

body.body:
## A spring Friday, but a chilly one ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRCkvLXfZJtbQJPgTt3PBUPR95NeRUhQdGQv4Ggg9L8Me/a00.jpg) Friday was quite nice, but the morning breeze made it clear to me that winter had just departed. And I felt it strongly. >Piątek całkiem fajny, ale poranne podmuchy wiatru dały mi do zrozumienia, że zima odeszła niedawno. I poczułem to mocno. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeCBdAqWjoK7adE6UkKcctocGittp9FbkNqwKjmA1qaVn/a01.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmemxNUHZTDR8AKfZv3gXAqG2GXSif5VbQcB2WTbB7EM5P/a02.jpg) The walk was monotonous, and the planned grilled chicken dinner was canceled. The wind was unpleasant, and the temperature was 13 degrees Celsius, so what was supposed to be the first spring picnic was moved indoors. >Spacer monotonny, a zaplanowane spożywanie kurczaka z rusztu zostało odwołane. Wiatr był nieprzyjemny a temperatura 13 stopni spowodowała, że obiad który miał być pierwszym wiosennym piknikiem, został przeniesiony do domu. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUJ3bfsVhxivvYZWu8Mb1Qa518cPsNnwLKFqpwd6zueko/a03.jpg) The birds were fed as usual, but today, unusually, they didn't get nuts, but instead received whole wheat bread with sunflower seeds. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to do all the shopping I wanted yesterday. But overall, the gang was happy. >Ptaszki tradycyjnie nakarmione, ale dzisiaj wyjątkowo nie dostały orzeszków, ale chleb razowy ze słonecznikiem. Niestety nie udało mi się wczoraj zrobić zakupów takich jak chciałem. Ale generalnie ferajna była zadowolona. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSid8QfU31yUW472ideqVmg8j9p4zSjoLXC4rinHcxqxK/g03.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmec8xhpNP5smxKeSXXGa48xBd366Aw74gL3rN5HvfJtgu/ornament_funny.png)
