## Training a CNN on CIFAR-10

Enough history. Let's build something real. **CIFAR-10**: 60,000 tiny (32x32) color images across 10 classes -- airplanes, cars, birds, cats, deer, dogs, frogs, horses, ships, trucks. It's a standard benchmark that's substantially harder than MNIST but still feasible to train on a laptop CPU in reasonable time:

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torchvision import datasets, transforms
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

transform_train = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.RandomHorizontalFlip(),
    transforms.RandomCrop(32, padding=4),
    transforms.ToTensor(),
    transforms.Normalize((0.4914, 0.4822, 0.4465), (0.2470, 0.2435, 0.2616))
])
transform_test = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.ToTensor(),
    transforms.Normalize((0.4914, 0.4822, 0.4465), (0.2470, 0.2435, 0.2616))
])

train_data = datasets.CIFAR10('.', train=True, download=True, transform=transform_train)
test_data = datasets.CIFAR10('.', train=False, download=True, transform=transform_test)
train_loader = DataLoader(train_data, batch_size=128, shuffle=True)
test_loader = DataLoader(test_data, batch_size=256)
```

Those normalization values `(0.4914, 0.4822, 0.4465)` and `(0.2470, 0.2435, 0.2616)` are CIFAR-10's per-channel mean and standard deviation, precomputed from the training set. Normalizing inputs to zero mean and unit variance helps training converge faster (we discussed why in episode #40 -- it keeps the loss landscape well-conditioned). The augmentations (`RandomHorizontalFlip` and `RandomCrop` with padding) create training variety from the limited dataset. A flipped car is still a car; a slightly shifted bird is still a bird. This is essentially free data ;-)

Now our model -- a compact CNN with batch normalization:

```python
class CIFAR10Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.features = nn.Sequential(
            # Block 1: 3 -> 32 channels
            nn.Conv2d(3, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            # Block 2: 32 -> 64 channels
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            # Block 3: 64 -> 128 channels
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(128), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(128, 10)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        return self.classifier(x)

model = CIFAR10Net()
print(f\

)
```

Notice `AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)` at the end of the feature extractor. This is a modern replacement for the traditional flatten-after-conv approach -- it averages each feature map down to a single value, regardless of the spatial size. This means the same architecture could handle different input resolutions without changing the classifier. The VGG/AlexNet approach of flattening to a huge vector and then connecting to a massive FC layer wastes parameters; global average pooling is what most modern architectures use in stead.

## The training loop

Standard PyTorch training with the pieces we assembled in episodes #42-43, plus one important addition -- tracking accuracy alongside loss:

```python
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.01)
scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(optimizer, T_max=30)
loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

for epoch in range(30):
    model.train()
    correct, total = 0, 0
    for X, y in train_loader:
        pred = model(X)
        loss = loss_fn(pred, y)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        correct += (pred.argmax(1) == y).sum().item()
        total += len(y)
    scheduler.step()

    if epoch % 10 == 0:
        model.eval()
        test_correct = 0
        with torch.no_grad():
            test_correct = sum(
                (model(X).argmax(1) == y).sum().item()
                for X, y in test_loader)
        print(f\

)
```

A few things to note here. We're using `nn.CrossEntropyLoss` -- the standard loss for multi-class classification. It combines log-softmax and negative log-likelihood into one numerically stable operation (the model outputs raw logits, not probabilities -- cross-entropy handles the softmax internally). This is different from the `nn.BCELoss` we used for binary classification; cross-entropy generalizes to any number of classes.

The **cosine annealing** scheduler gradually reduces the learning rate following a cosine curve, from 0.001 down to near-zero over 30 epochs. Combined with **AdamW** (the weight decay variant of Adam we covered in episode #41), this is the modern default recipe.

This compact architecture should reach roughly 88-90% test accuracy on CIFAR-10 in 30 epochs. State of the art is around 99% with much larger models, more augmentation, and weeks of GPU time. But 88-90% from a model you can train on a laptop in minutes? That's not bad at all.

## Transfer learning: standing on giants' shoulders

Here's the most practically important technique in all of modern deep learning. Training a CNN from scratch requires large datasets and significant compute. **Transfer learning** sidesteps both: take a model pretrained on ImageNet (1.4 million images, 1000 classes), remove the classification head, bolt on a new one that fits your task, and fine-tune on your much smaller dataset.

The reason this works is the feature hierarchy we discussed last episode. A ResNet trained on ImageNet has learned to detect edges in layer 1, textures in layer 2, object parts in the middle layers, and high-level concepts in the deep layers. Those features -- edges, textures, shapes -- are universal. They transfer remarkably well between tasks. A model trained to classify dogs and cars produces features that are useful for classifying medical X-rays, satellite photos, or manufacturing defects.

```python
from torchvision import models

# Load pretrained ResNet-18 (11.7M parameters, trained on ImageNet)
resnet = models.resnet18(weights=models.ResNet18_Weights.DEFAULT)

# Replace the final FC layer (was 512 -> 1000, now 512 -> 10)
resnet.fc = nn.Linear(512, 10)

# Freeze everything except the new classifier
for param in resnet.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False
for param in resnet.fc.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = True

trainable = sum(p.numel() for p in resnet.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
total = sum(p.numel() for p in resnet.parameters())
print(f\

)
```

With a frozen backbone, only 5,130 parameters need training (512 x 10 weights + 10 biases). That's 0.05% of the model. The other 99.95% -- all those carefully learned edge detectors, texture recognizers, and shape detectors -- stay exactly as ImageNet training left them. This is the model surgery technique from episode #44, now applied to a real pretrained model in stead of our toy example.

## Fine-tuning strategies

Freezing the backbone and training only the head is the simplest approach, but you can do better. The standard three-phase recipe:

**Phase 1 -- Frozen backbone, train head only.** A few epochs with just the classification head training. This gets the head roughly calibrated to the new task without disturbing the pretrained features.

**Phase 2 -- Unfreeze and train everything with a small learning rate.** Once the head has converged, unfreeze the backbone and train the entire model with a learning rate 10-100x smaller than Phase 1. This gently adapts the pretrained features to your specific task.

**Phase 3 (optional) -- Differential learning rates.** Use the parameter groups technique from episode #44 to set different learning rates for different depths. Early layers (edges, textures) rarely need changing; deeper layers (object parts, high-level concepts) might benefit from larger adjustments.

```python
# Phase 1: head only
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(resnet.fc.parameters(), lr=1e-3)

# Quick head calibration (5 epochs)
for epoch in range(5):
    for X, y in train_loader:
        loss = loss_fn(resnet(X), y)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()

# Phase 2: unfreeze everything, small learning rate
for param in resnet.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = True

optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW([
    {'params': resnet.conv1.parameters(), 'lr': 1e-5},
    {'params': resnet.layer1.parameters(), 'lr': 1e-5},
    {'params': resnet.layer2.parameters(), 'lr': 5e-5},
    {'params': resnet.layer3.parameters(), 'lr': 1e-4},
    {'params': resnet.layer4.parameters(), 'lr': 1e-4},
    {'params': resnet.fc.parameters(), 'lr': 1e-3},
], weight_decay=0.01)

# Fine-tune (15 epochs)
scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(optimizer, T_max=15)
for epoch in range(15):
    resnet.train()
    for X, y in train_loader:
        loss = loss_fn(resnet(X), y)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
    scheduler.step()

    if epoch % 5 == 0:
        resnet.eval()
        correct = sum(
            (resnet(X).argmax(1) == y).sum().item()
            for X, y in test_loader)
        print(f\

)
```

Having said that, for most practical applications you'll find that the simple freeze-then-unfreeze approach works surprisingly well. Differential learning rates are an optimization on top of something that already works. Start simple, add complexity only when the simpler version underperforms.

## Batch normalization in convolutional networks

We've mentioned `BatchNorm2d` a few times now but haven't really unpacked how it differs from the `BatchNorm1d` we used in earlier episodes. For convolutional layers, batch norm normalizes per *channel* across both the batch dimension and the spatial dimensions:

```python
# BatchNorm1d: normalizes over (batch,) for each feature
# Input shape: (N, C) -> normalize along N for each C
bn1d = nn.BatchNorm1d(64)
x_1d = torch.randn(32, 64)

)

# BatchNorm2d: normalizes over (batch, height, width) for each channel
# Input shape: (N, C, H, W) -> normalize along N, H, W for each C
bn2d = nn.BatchNorm2d(64)
x_2d = torch.randn(32, 64, 16, 16)
print(f\

)

# Each channel gets ONE mean and ONE variance computed across
# the entire batch AND all spatial positions
print(f\

)
# gamma (scale) and beta (shift), each of size (64,) -- one per channel
```

The intuition: if a \

filter produces high values at some spatial positions and low values at others, batch norm ensures the distribution of those values is stable across training batches. This prevents the internal covariate shift problem (the distribution of inputs to each layer changing as earlier layers update) that makes deep networks hard to train. Every modern CNN architecture uses batch norm (or a close relative like layer norm or group norm) between convolutions.

## Choosing an architecture in 2026

The landscape has settled considerably. Here's the practical decision tree:

**ResNet-18/34/50**: the default starting point. Well-understood, widely supported in every framework, good balance of accuracy and speed. Use ResNet-50 when accuracy matters most; ResNet-18 when you need speed or have limited compute. If you're not sure which architecture to use, use ResNet.

**EfficientNet**: scales width, depth, and resolution together using a compound scaling coefficient. More accurate than ResNet per FLOP, but more complex to understand and modify. Good when you need to squeeze maximum accuracy from limited compute.

**Vision Transformer (ViT)**: applies the transformer architecture (originaly from NLP) directly to image patches. Competitive with or better than CNNs on large datasets, but data-hungry -- needs massive pretraining or aggressive data augmentation to work well on smaller datasets. We'll cover transformers in depth later in this series, and then circle back to ViT specifically.

For small datasets with transfer learning, the architecture choice matters far less than you'd think. A pretrained ResNet-18 with proper fine-tuning often beats a pretrained EfficientNet-B7 that wasn't fine-tuned well. **Execution beats architecture selection.** Get the training pipeline right first -- data augmentation, learning rate schedule, proper validation -- and worry about architecture optimization later.

We touched on augmentations briefly in the CIFAR-10 example, but they deserve more attention because they're often the differnce between a mediocre model and a good one. Data augmentation creates synthetic training variety from your existing images:

body.body:
Blurry and low resolution images are one of the most common problems faced by creators, business owners, and everyday users online. A single unclear photo can weaken a website banner, a product listing, or even a family memory saved on an old phone. This is where [Image Upscaler Tools](https://grovers.io/blog/best-image-upscaler-tools/) have changed the game in 2026.

An AI image upscaler uses trained models to rebuild missing details and increase image resolution without the usual blur that older resize tools produce. Instead of simply stretching pixels, these tools predict what the image should look like at a higher resolution and recreate it in a natural way.

This article explains how image upscaling works, what to look for in a good tool, and reviews 7 of the most used AI image upscaler options available online this year. The goal is to give a clear, honest overview so readers can understand which tool fits which type of work.

![Best Image Upscaler Tools.png](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/8529c487cfff8b812d7f50f7592796c8c0da916492623b1b1f301de8a18d6ebd)

## How AI Image Upscaling Works

Traditional image resizing stretches pixels to make a picture bigger, which usually results in blur and loss of detail. AI image upscaling works differently. It uses deep learning models trained on millions of high resolution images to study patterns, textures, and edges.

When a low resolution image is uploaded, the AI predicts what the missing pixels should look like based on its training. This process is known as Super Resolution, and it is the core technology behind modern image upscale tools. Different models are often designed for different image types, such as portraits, product photos, illustrations, or scanned documents.

## Why Image Upscaling Has Become Important in 2026

Visual content continues to dominate online communication. Studies published by HubSpot and other content marketing reports have shown that posts with clear, high quality visuals receive significantly higher engagement than those with poor image quality. This is one reason why AI image upscale tools have grown in demand across industries.

Some of the common reasons people use these tools include:

*   Improving image quality without editing experience

*   Preparing product photos for ecommerce listings

*   Creating sharp visuals for social media and marketing

*   Restoring old or scanned family photos

*   Upscaling images for print, posters, and banners

*   Enhancing AI generated images for higher resolution output

These are general use cases and apply to both free image upscaler tools and paid professional software.

## Quick Overview of the Best Image Upscaler Tools

Below is a simple list version of the tools covered in this article, along with their main strengths and pricing type.

1.  **LetsEnhance:** Best for ecommerce and product images. Supports up to 16x upscaling. Offers a limited free plan. Paid plans start around $9 per month.

2.  **Topaz Gigapixel AI:** Best for professional photography and print work. Supports up to 6x upscaling. No free plan. Subscription based pricing.

3.  **VanceAI:** Best for quick online enhancement. Supports up to 8x upscaling. Free preview credits available. Paid plans start around $9.90 per month.

4.  **Upscale.media:** Best for beginners and simple online use. Supports up to 4x upscaling. Freemium model.

5.  **Pixelcut:** Best for creators and social media content. Offers high resolution export. Free plan available. Pro plan starts around $9.99 per month.

6.  **Upscayl:** Best free offline option. Supports up to 4x upscaling. Completely free and open source.

7.  **Bigjpg:** Best for anime and illustrations. Supports up to 4x upscaling. Free plan available. Paid plans start around $6 per month.

## The 7 Best Image Upscaler Tools in 2026

### 1. LetsEnhance

![LetsEnhance.webp](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/854bac86138f583c788883850bf65ba7567b6269473a6899fc39e2943dce7169)

LetsEnhance is a browser based AI image upscaler known for handling different image types through separate AI models. It includes modes for photos, product images, AI art, illustrations, and old scans. Each model is tuned for a specific content type, which helps keep the final image looking natural.

The tool supports upscaling up to 16x, which is higher than most online options. It also provides a public API through Claid, which is commonly used by ecommerce platforms for bulk image enhancement.

*   Upscaling up to 16x resolution

It includes several AI models such as Standard, High Fidelity, Low Resolution, Very Compressed, and Art and CG. These options allow users to pick the model based on the condition of their image. The software is known for detail reconstruction on portraits, landscapes, and large print projects.

**Pricing:** Moved to a subscription model in late 2025. Current pricing is listed on the official Topaz Labs website.

#### 4. Upscale.media

![Upscale.media.webp](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/394794d6ee51f9fcccaee402107bfd47804323459ec093f2b20b69ee5722ba8c)

Upscale.media is a simple online tool focused on fast, one click upscaling. It is often used for quick social media fixes, small design tasks, and general everyday needs. The interface is minimal and easy to use, which makes it suitable for beginners.

It supports upscaling up to 4x and works with common formats such as JPG, PNG, and WebP.

#### Key Features

*   One click upscaling

*   Quick browser based processing

*   Beginner friendly interface

*   Supports JPG, PNG, and WebP

*   Good for casual daily use

**Pricing:** Free credits for new users. Paid plans start around $7 for credit packs.

#### 5. Pixelcut

![Pixelcut.webp](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/2a3249e8edee7f95ca25237f8e6d5544af1a912d52286d0bc24de9961d29e999)

Pixelcut is a web and mobile tool that combines image upscaling with other creative features. Along with upscaling, it includes background removal, object cleanup, and basic editing tools. This makes it useful for creators who handle multiple design tasks in one workflow.

It is often used for social media posts, thumbnails, and product images.

#### Key Features

*   Online and mobile access

*   Background removal included

*   Object cleanup tools

*   High resolution export

*   Creator focused interface

**Pricing:** Free plan available. Pro plans start around $9.99 per month.

#### 6. Upscayl

![Upscayl.webp](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/0e93cb78dafd1e6389a726e1c97fd7212fcd1d0d9a18edd6addcafd3e4f7211e)

Upscayl is a free and open source desktop AI image upscaler. It runs completely offline on Windows, macOS, and Linux, which means images are never uploaded online. This makes it a strong option for users who care about privacy or work without a stable internet connection.

It uses Real ESRGAN and related open source models, which are also used in many other upscaling tools behind the scenes.

#### Key Features

*   Free and open source

*   Offline processing

*   Multiple AI model options

*   Works across all major operating systems

*   No watermark on output

**Pricing:** 100% free.

#### 7. Bigjpg

![Bigjpg.webp](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/db8c951d6e63fcc2bd3bf908d16b3b21ed8d4bcc3955cd871cb1875332610ddd)



Bigjpg is focused on anime, cartoons, and digital illustrations. It is not built for photography, but performs well on flat colors and clean lines, which are common in drawn content. It uses a cloud based system, so no software installation is required.

Artists and illustrators often use it to prepare their work for prints, wallpapers, or large format displays.

#### Key Features

*   Specialized anime and illustration upscaling

*   Smooth edge enhancement

*   Noise reduction for digital art

*   Cloud based processing

*   Batch upscaling on paid plans

**Pricing:** Free plan available. Paid plans start around $6 per month.

## What to Consider Before Choosing an Image Upscaler Tool

Different tools are designed for different needs, and picking the right one depends on the type of image being upscaled. A few factors that usually matter include:

*   **Image type:** Photos, portraits, illustrations, and AI art often need different models.

*   **Resolution support:** Some tools support up to 4x, while others allow upscaling image to 4k or even 16x.

*   **Processing location:** Online tools are quicker to access, while offline tools offer more privacy.

*   **Batch processing:** Useful for ecommerce sellers and teams working with many images at once.

*   **Pricing model:** Subscription, one time purchase, or free open source options.

*   **Output quality:** Some tools focus on faithful reconstruction, while others lean toward generative detail.

These points apply to almost every image upscaler online, whether free or paid.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid When Upscaling Images

A few mistakes can reduce the quality of an upscaled image, even when using a strong AI tool.

First, starting with an extremely small or heavily damaged image limits how much detail the AI can recover. Second, upscaling the same image multiple times can introduce small artifacts with each pass. Third, using a model designed for photos on an illustration, or the other way around, often produces unnatural results. Choosing the correct model for the image type usually makes a noticeable difference.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the best free image upscaler in 2026?

Upscayl is widely considered the strongest free AI image upscaler because it runs offline, has no watermark, and uses open source models. For a simple online option, Upscale.media is also commonly used.

### Can an image be upscaled to 4k for free?

Yes, several tools allow users to upscale image to 4k free, including Upscayl, Upscale.media, and the free tier of VanceAI. Free plans usually include credit limits or processing caps.

### How does an AI image upscaler actually work?

An AI image upscaler uses deep learning models trained on large datasets of high resolution images. Instead of stretching pixels like older resize methods, it predicts missing details and rebuilds them naturally. This process is known as Super Resolution and is the reason AI upscaled image results look sharper than traditional resizing.

## Final Thoughts

Image quality has become a key part of online presence in 2026. From ecommerce listings to social media posts and personal photo archives, clear visuals make a noticeable difference. Image Upscaler Tools simplify this process by using AI to rebuild detail and improve resolution without heavy editing.

Each tool reviewed in this article serves a slightly different purpose. Some are built for professional photography, others for quick online use, and a few focus on free or offline access. Understanding how these tools differ helps in picking the one that fits a specific image type and workflow.

body.title: Sisu: Road to Revenge (2025) || Movie Review
body.body:
![1000104662.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/Eokfzd3CBVwjb3KvGTKunMRBiKUFWZ8hVZCRunar53PLC88DtFxEP2CKKzZR3JhmU55.jpg) *
Beware not to anger the human spirit, for you do not know what power it possesses.
*
When I heard that **Sisu: Road to Revenge** was in the works, I was both surprised and excited. However, I was also a little worried, as I didn’t want the original film to be undermined by an unworthy sequel. It’s quite a common thing among directors or producers to ruin a great movie with a disappointing follow-up. I saw this movie a couple of days ago and I can say I wasn't disappointed in any way. It was a deserving sequel and I was impressed. My experience is going to be hard to forget because the ending of this movie made me so emotional. *Sisu: Road to Revenge* is an action, thriller and war film. It is also a good and satisfying revenge film. It was written and directed by Jalmari Helander with Jorma Tommila reprising his role as the main character alongside Richard Brake, Stephen Lang with other supporting characters. ![1000104682.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/Eo45qojhoxGzmtfsmHo4Qg2ZxgzrL1VLLdQD2brrtxTH2q9kHnZqw5z6GfG9Uk1rV6D.jpg) ![1000104660.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23wzv7s888wyqBpEhuG9YuzGbMgxNEBtWD8N24xQDtbZrU2mu6dgSkmk6ktq3GGme8En6.jpg) ![1000104685.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23yTWEmGNunehYk57EMnZDNbuYXFMtxEeuYoPxQmGj6m86JAsAAhdnNpatAYBswoZpHLG.jpg) This movie was set to continue from the initial sequel and enriched with a little bit of backstory. In 1946, in the aftermath of World War II, Finland surrendered the lands of Karelia to the Soviet Union as part of the peace treaty. Nearly five hundred thousand people were displaced from their homes and to never return ever again. ![1000104696.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/EoASvidCeMgJ4uX44tapcxjkY9o71v2AFgjMJofv7GsnkD9dMZJoyhEo7HZ9sfxoeEn.jpg) ![1000104688.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23tbRLXHHSzLz6Ux5rKyy5yysQLP2aDuJUQKp3NyWkpfMPNrsNEMMvyhEvCaVvuA7CVmQ.jpg) ![1000104689.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23tGZrJ1jpZsS7uwgvMzVdJCzdm31vgqtaFMhL1Hr3wEnoRS7BUPARr7ZuNwZ8xGLxPCz.jpg) Aatami Korpi, Finnish ex-commando, *”The man who refuse to die”* decided to cross the border into Karelia to visit his past where his family were brutally murdered during the war. Seeing his home looking abandoned brought back painful memories to him. Then he dismantled it and loaded every piece of his home into his truck with the intention of rebuilding it somewhere safe to honour the memories of his lovely family. ![1000104691.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23t7DFxpvyj18BNmcCfWUAyHUpFrDPdaBqp39ZHogVRDx2UASDs9YALE9ffUUWPU3fVa9.jpg) ![1000104690.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23t7B734RUXjzPiD4efGxw6MD3eX2vVCyeePWS1crmtF8a9EXYSyPGDeaxNQoys1ZiNsu.jpg) ![1000104692.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23tvCoTGZPo7fLr3kz4McJpfVC6VUU8VMZLsVUgW9KbFERErcoEZf17nNXEeydvsNQTL7.jpg) However, the Soviet authorities got to know about Aatami crossing the border to their territory. So a Nazi commander released the man who brutally butchered Aatami’s family, Yeagor Draganov from a prison in Siberia. This Commander promised Yeagor riches if only he could kill Aatami for the revenge of the Red Army troops in the Winter War he slaughtered. Will Yeagor succeed? #### My Review And Rating Helander did a fantastic job with this sequel and I was quite impressed with it. The writing was excellent and intriguing. I love how the plot was written which gave more insight on Aatami’s character and why he is particular about revenge. The narrative technique was engaging and captivating. I wasn't bored throughout the run time of the movie, instead I was on the edge of my seat, concerned about the main character dying. The directorial style was amazing. I love how every scene was well arranged and it gave the movie a relentless pacing and good escalation. Every scene had tension because of the brutal ambush, the aircraft chase, the dog close to danger, the old banged up truck, and the survival moments of the main character. Also, the movie was divided into chapters that came with its own unique gore and violence. With each chapter, it keeps getting better. The cinematography was so good that it made me feel nostalgic. It was a simple yet a vintage depiction of violence. I like that CGI was not depended on to portray all the violent and action parts. It was all made like the classic 80s and 90s action. Right from the start, the movie feels like it was done with a high budget. Is the impact it had on me, the gory scenes where it was convincing and realistic. Tommila is an amazing actor even without a single word being said by him throughout the movie, his performance is one of the best I have ever seen. His performance was solid, his mannerism, facial expression and grunts tell you everything you need to know. Stephen Lang as the antagonist was amazing! I loved and enjoyed his performance. The way he carried himself all through the movie was thrilling. Every single word he said, further aggravated the protagonist into his beast mode. This movie basically depicts how grief can change one, war and its aftermath, revenge, why justice needs to be served always and how the human spirit can be resilient. Rating this movie, I will give it 9 out of 10 stars. It was a wonderful movie. I enjoyed every bit of it and it was a deserving sequel to the initial installment. If you like the “one-man army” kind of movie, I'd encourage you to watch this movie and you won't be disappointed. https://youtu.be/VmStqCXIgio?si=jDfXL69HGTI7LiNC ![3yZiouw5jgtrj8RZntzpYvPkttnUNCNB3bKsugcDmKrZysEhsVCu7HmxWG7sYd9c3PJiWe24wRnpAB7HXq2WMvHX9AyxjgRuTY38KWSsv8...GFDdhx4UzPxqzjjpVMXNYgRDyspwo7pFw2RpyHZvde1tK7QLmYqnXBk9hDVg1dAooe2nLquVnXKjzS2uR5yQNqx1V5qutNgmqpFfKYLpS93ajRQosgFNPk3e1s.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23t7BFjADUCGjsLPt1YzFafTb9BeZ3Err5bNPwTi6RYNWED9TfZAhqAcZ8JCb2rGLLeT6.gif) *All images above are from the movie screenshots* *[Poster image source](https://pics.filmaffinity.com/Sisu_Road_to_Revenge-940529811-large.jpg)* *Thank you for visiting and supporting my blog* 🤗

## Hive in Cuba: Between Limitations and Real Opportunity

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdnaGAtxw37N9VSDw5BpmQJeXdjpWRtGv424HfHPzhARX/ahstubbs_havana_2535935_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/havana-back-street-2535935/)

---

In Cuba, accessing Hive is already a challenge before you even start growing.

I’ve been on this platform for about 9 months now (@vladimirmf). I started from zero, and with consistency, I’ve managed to grow to over 700 HP. It has been a slow process, but also a meaningful one. Hive has taught me a lot—not just about content creation, but about discipline, patience, and long-term vision.

But behind that growth, there is a reality that is not always visible.

Internet access here is expensive. Most people do not have fixed internet at home, and I am one of them. That means relying on mobile data or public WiFi spots, which already creates limitations.

On top of that, the electricity situation is very unstable. It is not uncommon to have outages that last up to 24 hours, followed by only 2 or 3 hours of service. Under these conditions, maintaining consistency on Hive becomes a real challenge.

My main tool is a OnePlus 3T from 2017, almost 9 years old. The battery is no longer reliable, and the camera also has focusing issues, which affects the quality of my photos. This has even limited my participation in some communities where image quality is important.

Even so, I keep going.

Because Hive is more than money. It is opportunity.

In Cuba, income levels are low, and many people earn around 6000–6500 CUP or even less. When you compare that with real living costs, the situation becomes very difficult.

A bag of bread costs between 350 and 400 CUP, and a family may need one every two days. A pound of pork ranges from 950 to 1100 CUP depending on the cut. A liter of cooking oil is around 1400 CUP.

Transportation is another major challenge. There are no regular buses or public transport systems available in many areas. The main option is private cars that operate as shared taxis. The price is usually per person, around 200 CUP for short distances within the city, because several passengers share the same car from a pickup point.

However, if someone hires the car privately as a taxi, the cost is much higher since the driver covers the entire trip alone. For example, from my neighborhood to the hospital—where doctors, nurses, and patients travel daily—a private taxi can cost around 2000 CUP. This is also affected by fuel prices, as gasoline in the informal market can reach up to 3000 CUP per liter due to scarcity.

When you add everything together—food, transport, basic needs—it becomes clear how difficult daily life is. Even professionals such as doctors and engineers often have to wait for hours at transport stops because they simply cannot afford to pay daily transport costs.

This is the context in which people try to grow, learn, and build something in Hive.

And this is where initiatives like BBH become meaningful.

The idea of supporting users with something like 0.40 HBD daily for 30 days (around 12 HBD total) may seem small, but in this reality it can make a real difference—especially if it helps users stay, learn, and power up instead of just spending.

More importantly, it aligns with a principle that many of us understand well: it is not about giving fish, but teaching how to fish.

Hive already has the potential to change lives. What many people need is guidance, consistency, and a small initial push to stay long enough to understand that potential.

From my experience, I can say this clearly: it works—but it is not easy.

And sometimes, even something as simple as having a functional device can make a big difference.

---

Special thanks to @bradleyarrow for supporting the community.

## Hive en Cuba: entre limitaciones y oportunidades reales

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdnaGAtxw37N9VSDw5BpmQJeXdjpWRtGv424HfHPzhARX/ahstubbs_havana_2535935_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/havana-back-street-2535935/)

---

En Cuba, acceder a Hive ya es un desafío incluso antes de empezar a crecer.

Llevo alrededor de 9 meses en la plataforma (@vladimirmf). Empecé desde cero y, con constancia, he logrado superar los 700 HP. Ha sido un proceso lento, pero significativo. Hive me ha enseñado mucho: no solo sobre creación de contenido, sino también sobre disciplina, paciencia y visión a largo plazo.

Pero detrás de ese crecimiento hay una realidad que no siempre se ve.

El acceso a internet aquí es costoso. La mayoría de las personas no tiene internet fijo en casa, y yo soy una de ellas. Eso significa depender de los datos móviles o de zonas WiFi públicas, lo cual ya impone limitaciones.

A esto se suma la situación eléctrica, que es muy inestable. No es raro tener apagones de hasta 24 horas y luego solo contar con 2 o 3 horas de servicio. En estas condiciones, mantener constancia en Hive se vuelve un verdadero reto.

Mi herramienta principal es un OnePlus 3T del 2017, con casi 9 años de uso. La batería ya no es confiable, y la cámara también tiene problemas de enfoque, lo que afecta la calidad de las fotos. Esto me ha limitado incluso en comunidades donde la fotografía es importante.

Aun así, sigo adelante.

Porque Hive es más que dinero. Es una oportunidad.

En Cuba, los niveles de ingreso son bajos, y muchas personas ganan alrededor de 6000–6500 CUP o incluso menos. Cuando se compara con el costo real de la vida, la situación se vuelve muy difícil.

Una bolsa de pan cuesta entre 350 y 400 CUP, y una familia puede necesitar una cada dos días. Una libra de carne de cerdo cuesta entre 950 y 1100 CUP según el corte. Un litro de aceite ronda los 1400 CUP.

El transporte es otro gran problema. No existen autobuses regulares ni un sistema de transporte público estable en muchas zonas. La opción principal son los carros particulares que funcionan como taxis compartidos. El precio suele ser por persona, alrededor de 200 CUP para trayectos cortos dentro de la ciudad, ya que varias personas comparten el mismo carro desde un punto de recogida.

Sin embargo, si alguien alquila el carro como taxi privado, el costo es mucho mayor, ya que el conductor asume todo el viaje. Por ejemplo, desde mi barrio hasta el hospital—donde médicos, enfermeros y pacientes se trasladan a diario—un taxi privado puede costar alrededor de 2000 CUP. Esto también está influido por el precio del combustible, ya que la gasolina en el mercado informal puede llegar a 3000 CUP por litro debido a la escasez.

Cuando se suma todo—alimentación, transporte, necesidades básicas—queda claro lo difícil que es la vida diaria. Incluso profesionales como médicos e ingenieros muchas veces tienen que esperar horas en paradas porque simplemente no pueden pagar el transporte todos los días.

Este es el contexto en el que las personas intentan crecer, aprender y construir algo en Hive.

Y aquí es donde iniciativas como BBH cobran sentido.

La idea de apoyar a usuarios con algo como 0.40 HBD diarios durante 30 días (unos 12 HBD en total) puede parecer pequeña, pero en esta realidad puede marcar una diferencia real, especialmente si ayuda a los usuarios a quedarse, aprender y hacer power up en lugar de solo gastar.

Más importante aún, se alinea con un principio que muchos entendemos bien: no se trata de regalar el pescado, sino de enseñar a pescar.

Hive ya tiene el potencial de cambiar vidas. Lo que muchas personas necesitan es orientación, constancia y un pequeño impulso inicial que les permita quedarse el tiempo suficiente para entender ese potencial.

Desde mi experiencia puedo decirlo con claridad: funciona, pero no es fácil.

Y a veces, incluso algo tan simple como tener un dispositivo funcional puede marcar una gran diferencia.

---

body.title: Splinterlands: Sometimes speed is all you need
body.body:
Splinterlands is a complex game, and it allows for various cards and strategies. Each fight is different as there are various rulesets applied, and this can give specific cards an advantage depending on how you use them. In this post, I talk about a great battle where I saw a battle where I won because I used the correct archon.

## Rule Set, Battle, and Plan

<center>![rule set.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jfang003/EoEiitcuHyTw72J4z7SLrDQTxHYZgWWca2bvmmqfrrCUuHuh5pFCDZTHNPPj3BWeu7p.png)</center>
The rulesets this time are Arcane Dampening and Aim True. This means all monsters gain the void ability, and monsters can't miss. There is also 35 mana available, and I can use any [splinter](https://leofinance.io/@leoglossary/leoglossary-splinter) except for water or death.

This is an interesting fight because nothing can miss, and it only makes sense to use melee or ranged monsters.

|Splinter|Mana Cost|Position|Reason|
|---|---|---|---|
|Barthalamas|6|Summoner|+1 speed|
|Frankarsgard|7|1st||
|Chaos Furybringer|6|2nd|Reach|
|Sturdy Axe Warden|8|3rd||
|A'lan Musketeer|8|4th|Double Strike|
|Total Mana:|35|||

My summoner is Barthalamas for +1 speed. I have Frankarsgard as my tank. After that is Chaos Furybringer as my backup tank with reach. Finally, I have two ranged damage dealers, and A'lan also has double strike.

The focus of this lineup is to keep my monsters alive while dealing damage and outlasting my opponent. I will be relying on the increased speed to wipe out my opponent before he wipes me out. The combination of all my monsters can easily kill off a few monsters if my opponent doesn't have taunt. 

### Round 1


![round 1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jfang003/EoAbAQ6J852dtYprK8FYvSSAcvXhZYe94yqewr3HqF7wsxBzQz29Q2V4DmUuvCVyDXT.png)

At first glance, I think that this match is my win. My opponent may have a tank with heal, but my monsters will be faster than his, and they also can't miss. My opponent just doesn't seemt o have enough damage to overcome that speed advantage.

### Round 3
![round 3.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jfang003/23u677HRydei7QcwJ48pMEcx4YoBDLRVS2E1v6VPxFDD3fzNZRozYbbDWbKc7w7zaWHG4.png)
A few rounds later, I have lost one monster, but my opponent is down 2 monsters. There is no way for my opponent to overcome the speed advantage. 

![conclusion.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jfang003/23uFXmqBz5n5TBJsyYkapuSvXBeL4StJHxN7VQpDp8QjbW3AwoXTT1kV6B5iR1RN5qq3d.png)
I won later that round.

## Conclusion
The battle did go exactly as planned. Relying on speed was the best choice because we couldn't miss, and magic monsters are not as effective. I was able to move before my opponent, and this gave me a great advantage over my opponent. There were times when some of his monsters could not attack before they died.

You can see my entire match [here](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_a5ea64f78b4973158a2994b63e9e908f?ref=jfang003).

What did you think of my match? Was there anything you would have done differently? I think it is quite interesting to see how different players use the same card.

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@jfang003/splinterlands-sometimes-speed-is-all-you-need-j9r)

title.title: Cuando Nadie Aplaude #10 — La persona que lo intenta otra vez después de fallar. [Esp/Eng]
title.body:
* * *

Hola comunidad @holos-lotus hoy continuo con la serie, **Cuando Nadie Aplaude** en ella pretendo mostrar aquellas situaciones poco reconocidas, pero muy humanas y que forman parte de nuestra vida

* * *

## La persona que lo intenta otra vez después de fallar  

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma8rXHMaYTZe2GohM9dWKwMuHZ7kiGg3yQZYchShJRvaz/stocksnap_cold_2557518_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/cold-weather-winter-hoodie-jacket-2557518/)

---

Hay momentos en los que fallar no es lo más difícil.  

Lo más difícil es lo que viene después.  

El silencio.  
La duda.  
La sensación de haber retrocedido.  

Y esa pregunta que aparece sin avisar:  

—¿Vale la pena volver a intentarlo?  

---

**La persona que lo intenta otra vez después de fallar** no siempre tiene confianza.  

No siempre está segura.  
No siempre se siente fuerte.  

Pero hay algo que la empuja a dar un paso más, incluso cuando todo dentro de ella le dice que se detenga.  

---

Fallar deja marcas.  

A veces visibles.  
A veces internas.  

Hace que uno se cuestione decisiones, capacidades, incluso caminos completos.  

Y sin embargo…  

algunas personas vuelven a empezar.  

---

No con la misma energía.  
No con la misma ingenuidad.  

Pero sí con algo más profundo:  
experiencia.  

---

Tengo 25 años y cada vez entiendo más que volver a intentar no es repetir el mismo camino.  

Es caminarlo de otra forma.  

Con más cuidado.  
Con más conciencia.  
Con más respeto por lo que uno ya vivió.  

---

Volver a intentar no siempre es visible.  

No siempre se anuncia.  
No siempre se comparte.  

A veces sucede en silencio.  

En decisiones pequeñas.  
En pasos discretos.  
En intentos que nadie ve.  

---

Si lo pensara como una fotografía, no sería una imagen de triunfo.  

Sería algo mucho más sencillo:  

Alguien atándose los zapatos.  
Levantándose temprano.  
Abriendo otra vez algo que una vez cerró.  

---

Nada espectacular.  

Pero lleno de intención.  

---

La persona que lo intenta otra vez después de fallar no recibe aplausos inmediatos.  

Porque el mundo suele celebrar los resultados, no los procesos.  

Nadie ve el momento en que decide no rendirse.  
Nadie mide el esfuerzo emocional de volver a empezar.  

---

Y aun así, lo hace.  

Con dudas.  
Con miedo.  
Con cierta fragilidad.  

Pero lo hace.  

---

Quizás ahí está la diferencia.  

No en no caer…  
sino en decidir levantarse incluso cuando nadie lo espera.  

---

Volver a intentar también implica aceptar que puede fallar otra vez.  

Y aun así, avanzar.  

Eso requiere una forma de valentía que no siempre se reconoce.  

---

Porque el mundo no siempre recompensa el intento.  

Pero el intento cambia a la persona.  

La hace más consciente.  
Más resistente.  
Más real.  

---

Tal vez crecer también es entender que fallar no es el final de algo,  
sino parte del proceso de construirlo mejor.  

---

Y aunque nadie lo aplauda…  

intentarlo otra vez, después de haber fallado,  
también es una forma de seguir creyendo.  

---

Con esto termina este capítulo y me despido. Díganme en los comentarios que les pareció y si quieren apoyar será bien recibido.

Las imágenes utilizadas son de Pixabay y utilizo Google Translate para la versión en inglés.

* * *

🇬🇧 *English Version*

* * *

### When No One Applauds #10  

### The Person Who Tries Again After Failing  

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma8rXHMaYTZe2GohM9dWKwMuHZ7kiGg3yQZYchShJRvaz/stocksnap_cold_2557518_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/cold-weather-winter-hoodie-jacket-2557518/)

---

There are moments when failing is not the hardest part.  

The hardest part is what comes after.  

The silence.  
The doubt.  
The feeling of having gone backwards.  

And that question that appears without warning:  

—Is it worth trying again?  

---

**The person who tries again after failing** is not always confident.  

Not always sure.  
Not always strong.  

But there is something that pushes them to take one more step, even when everything inside tells them to stop.  

---

Failure leaves marks.  

Sometimes visible.  
Sometimes internal.  

It makes you question decisions, abilities, even entire paths.  

And yet…  

some people begin again.  

---

Not with the same energy.  
Not with the same innocence.  

But with something deeper:  
experience.  

---

I am 25 years old, and I understand more and more that trying again is not about repeating the same path.  

It is about walking it differently.  

With more care.  
With more awareness.  
With more respect for what you have already lived.  

---

Trying again is not always visible.  

It is not always announced.  
It is not always shared.  

Sometimes it happens in silence.  

In small decisions.  
In quiet steps.  
In attempts that no one sees.  

---

If I thought of it as a photograph, it would not be an image of victory.  

It would be something much simpler:  

Someone tying their shoes.  
Waking up early.  
Opening again something they once closed.  

---

Nothing spectacular.  

But full of intention.  

---

The person who tries again after failing does not receive immediate applause.  

Because the world tends to celebrate results, not processes.  

No one sees the moment they decide not to give up.  
No one measures the emotional effort of starting again.  

---

And still, they do it.  

With doubt.  
With fear.  
With a certain fragility.  

But they do it.  

---

Maybe that is where the difference lies.  

Not in never falling…  
but in choosing to rise even when no one expects it.  

---

Trying again also means accepting that it might fail once more.  

And still moving forward.  

That requires a kind of courage that is not always recognized.  

---

Because the world does not always reward the attempt.  

But the attempt changes the person.  

It makes them more aware.  
More resilient.  
More real.  

---

Maybe growing up is also understanding that failure is not the end of something,  
but part of the process of building it better.  

---

And even if no one applauds it…  

trying again after failing  
is also a way of still believing.  

---

With this, this chapter comes to an end, and I say goodbye. Let me know in the comments what you think, and if you want to support it, it will be greatly appreciated.

The images used are from Pixabay, and I use Google Translate for the English version.

## Greetings, citizens of Praetoria and fellow Hiveans! 🖐️

I just finished one of the most prestigious and challenging tournaments in Splinterlands: the Gloridax Wild Diamond Invitational GF. This tournament isn't just any tournament; it's an arena where only the best Gold Foil cards can compete, and in the Diamond league, the slightest mistake means instant defeat.

As a Wild format tournament, we saw a deadly combination of legendary Alpha/Beta cards paired with the latest mechanics from Rebellion.

Competing in the Gold Foil Diamond format requires a very specific strategy. Because the number of players with GF Diamonds is limited, the opponents are typically whales and veteran players with very sharp strategies.

## ⚔️ The Strategy: Riding the Dragons

As the name suggests, Gloridax, the Dragon faction, is the key to this tournament. The flexibility to choose additional elements makes my defense very flexible.

## 💡 My Reflections on the \

Meta 

Playing in the current Wild Gold Foil format really tests the depth of our collections. Players who still hold onto Untamed and Dice Gold Foil cards have a huge advantage, especially with cards like Yodin Zaku or Llama still dominant in certain rulesets.

**However**, Rebellion mechanics like Tactical Attacks are starting to show their teeth to counter these old metas.

The Gloridax Wild Diamond Invitational GF tournament is always a benchmark for how far our decks have progressed. While challenging, the SPS prizes and prestige are always worth the effort.

## The Story That Stayed With Me
## Silver Bloggers Chronicles Prompt #43

- - -

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY4gLaqPnmNu16WPYjjRQVMZhrVTQKgGQqDykJWLu4aXX/pezibear_child_857021_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/child-girl-book-read-reading-857021/)

---

Hello @silver-bloggers community.

What was your absolute favorite story when you were a child?

When I think about my childhood, there are many moments that have faded with time, but some stories remain intact, as if they had quietly settled somewhere inside me.

One of them is *The Little Prince*.

- - -

I don’t remember the exact day I first encountered it, but I clearly remember the place. I was at home, in a quiet afternoon that felt slower than usual. The light came softly through the window, and I had found a copy of the book among other things that had been in the house for a long time.

At that age, I didn’t fully understand everything I was reading. But somehow, I felt that the story was speaking to me in a different way.

It wasn’t just a tale. It felt like a conversation.

- - -

What stayed with me the most was not a single scene, but a feeling — the idea that what is truly important is often invisible. That people carry entire worlds inside them, even when nothing seems obvious on the surface.

Looking back, I think that story shaped the way I began to see others. It taught me, in a quiet and subtle way, to look beyond appearances, to listen more carefully, to try to understand what is not always said.

Perhaps that is why, years later, I found my path in medicine.

Because caring for someone is not only about what can be seen, but also about what must be understood.

- - -

There were other stories, of course. Adventures, school readings, fragments of tales that came and went. But *The Little Prince* stayed.

Not because I understood it completely, but because I grew into it.

And even now, when I return to its pages, I discover something new — as if the story had been waiting patiently for me to catch up with it.

- - -

Some stories accompany us for a while.

Others, quietly, become part of who we are.

Thank you for reading.
See you in the words.

🇪🇦 En Español

## La historia que se quedó conmigo
## Silver Bloggers Chronicles Prompt #43

- - -

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY4gLaqPnmNu16WPYjjRQVMZhrVTQKgGQqDykJWLu4aXX/pezibear_child_857021_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/child-girl-book-read-reading-857021/)

---

Hola comunidad @silver-bloggers.

¿Cuál fue tu historia favorita cuando eras niño?

Cuando pienso en mi infancia, hay muchos momentos que el tiempo ha ido borrando poco a poco, pero algunas historias permanecen intactas, como si se hubieran quedado viviendo en algún rincón de mí.

Una de ellas es *El Principito*.

- - -

No recuerdo el día exacto en que lo encontré por primera vez, pero sí recuerdo el lugar. Estaba en casa, en una tarde tranquila que parecía avanzar más despacio de lo habitual. La luz entraba suave por la ventana, y encontré el libro entre otras cosas que llevaban tiempo allí.

A esa edad, no comprendía todo lo que leía. Pero de alguna manera sentía que la historia me hablaba de una forma distinta.

No era solo un cuento. Era como una conversación.

- - -

Lo que más se quedó conmigo no fue una escena en particular, sino una sensación — la idea de que lo verdaderamente importante muchas veces es invisible. Que las personas llevan mundos enteros dentro, incluso cuando nada lo hace evidente.

Mirándolo ahora, creo que esa historia influyó en la forma en que empecé a ver a los demás. Me enseñó, de manera silenciosa, a mirar más allá de lo evidente, a escuchar con más atención, a intentar comprender lo que no siempre se dice.

Tal vez por eso, años después, encontré mi camino en la medicina.

Porque cuidar a alguien no es solo ver, sino también entender.

- - -

Hubo otras historias, claro. Aventuras, lecturas de la escuela, fragmentos de cuentos que iban y venían. Pero *El Principito* se quedó.

No porque lo entendiera por completo, sino porque crecí con él.

Y aún hoy, cuando vuelvo a sus páginas, descubro algo nuevo — como si la historia hubiera estado esperando pacientemente a que yo la alcanzara.

- - -

Algunas historias nos acompañan por un tiempo.

Otras, en silencio, se convierten en parte de quienes somos.

Gracias por leerme.
Nos encontramos en las palabras.

Las imagenes son de pixabay y la traducción al ingles fue hecha en DeepL Translate.

title.title: Hive Philippines Travel and Nature Photography #1139 - by Allmonitors
title.body:
#1139 - City Lights Shots at Night Somewhere in Makati for Friday. 

Hello my wonderful Hive family worldwide! TGIF and Happy Friday to everyone! We have finally reached the end of the work week, and it is time to celebrate. Let go of any stress and look forward to a relaxing weekend ahead. Have a safe and happy weekend.

Moving now to our daily shots one beautiful evening when my wife and I and son Joaquin were at a high-rise hotel in Makati. We were here as visitors invited to a dinner by my wife's relatives. They had been staying at this place for a few days and were kind enough to invite us over to join them for a meal. 
![1000017264.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/allmonitors/23tkfznRt53k7DibNgHXxwYBZzqAJVVNn8rntiJJ1PoEPVkMnQbnnVtBA5QSEsDiVMkS3.jpg)

When we arrived, the atmosphere was grand. Before we had dinner, our relatives insisted that we take a tour of their hotel floor first. They wanted to show us the amenities and the stunning views that the building had to offer. 
![1000017263.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/allmonitors/Eo44nRhfhmRq9Av9pL7DPnTwYDiUjkiggZvYcDK6h9M69y7Wku2x9RokSw6Pg4LJtjz.jpg)

They led us to a specific viewing area like an observation deck or lounge where it's open with winds sometimes. We were mesmerized by the sight of Makati City at night. It was a breathtaking panorama of urban life. The scene below was colorful bright lights that stretch endlessly.
![1000017265.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/allmonitors/23tGZbpKxoseMbRRrQHiJKChmie69MFuic1mYfBPfKJcrC5CT5rjsimZssTsyYRi2krwm.jpg)

Looking down, we could see the busy roads of the city. They looked like rivers of lights as cars and motorcycles and other vehicles moved along the roads. The traffic was like a sense of constant movement. It was fascinating to watch the tiny vehicles navigate streets from a high vantage point.
![1000017266.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/allmonitors/23t7BBwSMWryAnPQDStLsF858UhMuoZB8z9Q7ZYZfuyeSB723Txmw7SiBHuPKRPvogqg9.jpg)

There was the Pasig River wounding its way through the concrete landscape, it's dark and mysterious against the bright city lights. We spent a good amount of time here just staring, pointing out landmarks like the Powerplant Mall and appreciating the night beauty of the metropolitan.
![1000017261.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/allmonitors/23tbPY11v5qDZSmapsQhTt6kPJN3YhY6efv7CXhBVu7YFZj8FzsgxYGXdVYEwg355vie6.jpg)

![1000017262.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/allmonitors/Eo6D951y8Ur4uJ7qLNQDZD8jRGrBD47z7819n9jJ4DUUJzMo8pjeqWn8zjrPU3NtoGF.jpg)

Follow me on my nature travels.
Shot taken in Makati, Philippines.

<center>Image/s were shot using Samsung Z5 flip phone. ~rex</center>

title.title: Be Careful Of What Your Normalize
title.body: >\n\nA lot of people have accepted a lot of things in their lives without even questioning them, and they are suddenly becoming a standard for them. Whether negative or positive, what you normalize in your life has the ability to shape your mindset, your thought pattern, behaviour, and ultimately your future. This is why you have to be intentional to know what you accept as \

in your life. What you welcome in your life has the power to remain. But much more than that, they can also affect a lot of things about you.

<center>![pexels-shvets-production-9772692.jpg](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmSTzBYZm5gzjAGCNr4pzocNm7aaemfoUWoFFDEV9hL82Q/pexels-shvets-production-9772692.jpg)</center>

<center><sub>Image from [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/studio-shot-of-girl-writing-no-word-on-glass-9772692)</sub></center>

You may not notice this, but the truth is that the small compromises you allow, can become a major limitation over time. When you begin to normalize unhealthy habits, negative things, low standards, you will gradually begin to lower your expectations for yourself. When that starts to happen, what once felt wrong and unacceptable will begin to look normal, and acceptable to you. And once something begins to feel normal, it will become difficult to change it. It may start with \

but before you know it, it will become part of you. This is why self-awareness is very important. You have to regularly check your attitude, your environment, your habits, and even your mindset to ensure that you are not accepting what is holding you back. Here, we shall take a look at what not to normalize at all. The first one is that you should not normalize making excuses for failure. When someone tries something and does not succeed at it, they may be quick to look for excuses to give to make themself feel good temporarily. But what they fail to understand is that it also prevents growth. If you always blame circumstances or other people for whatever happens, instead of taking responsibilities, you will not improve and you will not grow. Making excuses as normal will only keep you at a spot. I am not saying that you should be perfect, but you have to learn to take responsibilities when you make mistakes, so that you can learn from them and become better. The second one is not to normalize laziness, lack of discipline, and procrastination. It may feel comfortable to delay a task that you need to do, or to avoid putting efforts, but at the end, it will destroy progress. On the same hand, when you always postpone what you are to do today to a later day, you are delaying your progress. It is discipline that will help you to build success. But when you constantly choose comfort over taking responsibilities, you will not only weaken your potentials, but you will slowly lose discipline. Do not allow yourself to feel too comfortable to the point that you feel that you do not have a need to take steps. When you start to welcome procrastinating your actions, before you know it, it will become a pattern for you, and it will not be good.
![pexels-picasjoe-11352518 (1).jpg](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmQVEaom9by1cPrpoRwsTkCVG5SrSrqAmmj4fVkGM5uZWz/pexels-picasjoe-11352518%20%281%29.jpg)
Image from [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/woman-expressing-refusal-11352518)
The third one is; do not normalize negative thoughts. Your most dominant thought has a way of affecting a lot of things about you; from your attitude, to your actions, to your character, and even to your future. What you repeatedly think and tell yourself will become your belief system. If you normalize negative thoughts, you will begin to doubt yourself, and you will eventually become a limitation for yourself. But if you want to make progress and experience success, then you have to make positive thoughts your lifestyle. The last point is; do not normalize toxic relationship and poor influence. The people you allow into your life can influence your mindset in ways that you may never imagine. Anyone that would disrespect you, create negativity around you, or make you think lowly of yourself is not supposed to be allowed into your life. If you come in contact with someone and your life does not feel better, that means they are not a positive influence on you, and you should stay clear off them. Try to set clear boundaries of who and what you allow in your life. To grow and achieve success in life, you must be very intentional about what you accept. ***Thanks for reading***
Peace on y'all

## English 🇬🇧

There are places that feel like they belong to a different reality, and today was definitely one of those days. Being at Disneyland Paris is not just about rides or attractions, it’s about stepping into a world that was designed to make you forget everything else for a while. From the moment you walk in and see the architecture, the colors, and the details everywhere, you realize this place was built with a level of precision that goes far beyond entertainment. It’s like entering a perfectly controlled system where every variable is tuned to create a specific emotional response.  

Standing in front of the castle was one of those moments that hit differently. It’s something you’ve seen countless times in movies or images, but being there in person changes everything. The scale, the atmosphere, even the weather adds to the experience. It wasn’t a sunny postcard day, but somehow the cloudy sky made it feel even more cinematic. It’s interesting how sometimes imperfections in conditions actually enhance the perception of a place instead of taking away from it.  

Inside the attractions, everything becomes even more immersive. The level of detail in the scenes, the lighting, the characters… it’s not random at all. It’s engineered storytelling. Each space is carefully designed to guide your attention, to control what you feel, and to build tension or excitement at the right moment. As someone who tends to analyze systems, I couldn’t help but see this as a masterclass in how design and experience can be tightly coupled. This is not chaos, this is controlled imagination at its finest.  

But beyond all that analysis, what really matters is the feeling. There’s something simple and genuine about being there, like reconnecting with a version of yourself that didn’t overthink everything. Just walking around, observing, and enjoying the moment without needing to optimize anything… that’s probably the real magic of this place.  

## Español 🇪🇸

Hay lugares que se sienten como si pertenecieran a otra realidad, y hoy definitivamente fue uno de esos días. Estar en Disneyland París no se trata solo de juegos o atracciones, sino de entrar a un mundo diseñado para hacerte olvidar todo lo demás por un momento. Desde que entras y ves la arquitectura, los colores y los detalles en cada rincón, te das cuenta de que este lugar fue construido con un nivel de precisión que va mucho más allá del entretenimiento. Es como entrar a un sistema perfectamente controlado donde cada variable está ajustada para generar una respuesta emocional específica.  

Estar frente al castillo fue uno de esos momentos que se sienten diferentes. Es algo que has visto muchas veces en películas o imágenes, pero estar ahí en persona cambia todo. La escala, la atmósfera, incluso el clima influyen en la experiencia. No fue un día soleado de postal, pero de alguna forma el cielo nublado lo hizo sentir más cinematográfico. Es curioso cómo a veces las condiciones imperfectas pueden mejorar la percepción de un lugar en lugar de afectarla negativamente.  

Dentro de las atracciones, todo se vuelve aún más inmersivo. El nivel de detalle en las escenas, la iluminación, los personajes… nada es al azar. Es narrativa diseñada. Cada espacio está cuidadosamente pensado para guiar tu atención, controlar lo que sientes y generar tensión o emoción en el momento adecuado. Desde una perspectiva más analítica, es como una clase magistral de cómo el diseño y la experiencia pueden estar completamente integrados. No es caos, es imaginación controlada en su máxima expresión.  

Pero más allá de todo ese análisis, lo que realmente importa es la sensación. Hay algo simple y genuino en estar ahí, como reconectar con una versión de ti mismo que no sobrepiensa todo. Solo caminar, observar y disfrutar el momento sin necesidad de optimizar nada… probablemente esa es la verdadera magia de este lugar.

All you have to do, for a chance of winning one is 
- write a freewrite based on the @Daily.Prompt

Every day **three** of the best daily freewrites will be awarded **one** HiveSBI share. 
<sub>Not sure what Hive SBI is? [Find out more here](https://docs.hivesbi.com/)</sub>

What are you waiting for?



# <center>Today's #DailyPrompt is</center>

# <center>it’s not that hard</center>

...

How to freewrite...

- Set your timer for 5 minutes
- Start writing
- Use the hashtag #freewrite #dailyprompt
- Publish your piece (include a link to this post if you wish)
- Copy and paste your URL into the comment section of **this post**.
<sup>Or, if you don't want to publish your freewrite, just copy and paste as a comment under the prompt post.</sup>
- What if you want to write for longer than five minutes? No problem! There are no rules... 

except...

<sub>If you are running a contest you want to be listed here, let @felt.buzz know.</sub>

# Writing help

- A free app: Grammarly. A lot of us are not native English speakers and I am finding it a helpful app. It will underline spelling and grammar mistakes. Remember that it is not always right -especially if you use complex sentence structures. [Here is the link](https://app.grammarly.com/)
- Remember [The Most Dangerous Writing App](https://www.squibler.io/dangerous-writing-prompt-app). You set the time - 5 min - and start typing. Don’t stop!!! It will destroy what you wrote if you stop for more than 3 seconds - and backspace does not count as writing on the app. If you are prone to stop and think - this app forces you to keep going. You can make corrections after the 5 minutes are over.
- A timer. Egg timer is a free tool you can use on your desktop to set a time. This is useful for our freewrites or if you want to work in blocks of time and then take a break. [Here is the link](https://e.ggtimer.com/)

title.body:

Hello hive friends. Hope everyone doing great today where ever part of the world you are right now.. today I will share to you my pet snail in my little pond..I have a lots of apple snail, they are the one who clean my aquarium.. they eat the left over food of my fish in the aquarium.. since they are so many of them, i'm giving some to my friends who also have aquarium.. apple snail are great to put in aquarium even if you don't clean you're aquarium daily.. especially for those who have aquascape with aqua plants inside the aquarium.. because apple snails also eat the algae that grows on the leaves of the aqua plants..


![1000387421.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/blueoctopus/23vhwwERuEA33bACLBDCiLDzq7ECyfEk3YG6y6LC4GfKLhUZuSXTN6e2awCwYabAZf7Xn.jpg)

Apple snail multiply quickly, just put them in an aquarium or, even in small pond as long as they eat they will multiply quickly,, one egg laying will quickly produces over a hundred snails..

title.title: Квітник
title.body:
Мій цибульково-півонієвий квітничок біля веранди трішки заріс бур'янами. А коли почала тут прополювати, то нарешті перерахувала свої квіточки і переконалась, що всі на місці.
Так, після нашого переїзду ця клумбочка складалася спонтанно. Бо хотілося пошвидше навести лад у давно закинутому дворі, де майже 5 років ніхто не жив. За старими потребами, щоб відгородити квіти від курей, тут стояв паркан. А за ним вже й квітів не видно, - зарослі малини та кропиви... От і стали ми розбирати всі ці дикі зарості. А я тимчасом планувала, де і що посадити, та замовляла насіння і саджанці квітів.

![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valentinalife/Eo8UjexX8upVekfGQBnfY152xCRYrxbW8GgSjw3GfuWYN1uheABrcZJ8HynWFdvw57x.jpg)

Так і народилася ось ця \

частинка квітника. Тут багато нарцисів, тюльпанів, аліумів і інших цибулькових квіточок. А основою клумби стали пересаджені старезні півонії різних сортів. Пізніше тут будуть висаджені ще й цибулинки гладіолусів.

![5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valentinalife/23w2guXu8DsBcjWNJcKmR2DM99MznNBBQfLgbsLX8YoXrGEhhxhJtbg4BP4sskYS8LWDY.jpg)

А тимчасом чекаю з нетерпінням, коли розпустяться мої улюблені алліуми. Деякі мають цьогоріч вже по кілька квітконосів. Деякі - почали давати діток цибулинок, які цвістимуть наступного року. Тож - чекаємо!

![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valentinalife/EoAc9y2DFChGsD63XxJGrrd3pfkV3jjQF6AG5s83dzuzdyCyeySzqUYuXeqF2CwprLj.jpg)

![3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valentinalife/Eo8RtEmp1wCRXdHheEW8qKAsqGFTKFgZv1F48khV9pdXYyeKNAyz7sVeSVdw7hSCaWt.jpg)

![4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valentinalife/23tvcMcLupvvqh2Xgx3K85NZqGSKn2bMJrRoLdTymDw9GqAZct65HtA3F6GyaHqjPujpQ.jpg)

title.title: My Tiny Underwater World: Colorful Fish and Snail Behind the Curtain of Duckweed
title.body: /> Welcome to my backyard❗ Today, I want to show you my favorite hobby. We have three small ponds in our backyard. They are peaceful little places where I can watch nature up close. 😊 In these ponds, we breed many kinds of small fish. We have colorful guppies, jumpy mollies, tiny tetras, and elegant angelfish. We also have apple snails that crawl slowly along the bottom and on the surface. 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 Let's take a look inside the pond When you look into the water, it feels like a secret garden or more like another world. Here is what makes our ponds special, the floating greenery. 💚 The surface of the pond is covered with tiny green plants called duckweed. They look like little green stars floating on top of the water. Think of it as a floating curtain. When you draw it, it reveals a magical world. 😀

/> If you look closely at the green mossy plants, you might see an apple snail. They have round, golden shells and like to munch on the greenery. * * * * * * On the bottom, there are large, dark brown leaves. These leaves make the water look like tea. They give the fish a safe place to hide and rest.
/> * * * * * * When the sun shines, the water sparkles ✨ You can see the bright colors of the fish as they swim through the shadows of the plants.

/> Our fish are very active. In the photos, you can see a bright golden fish with a long, flowy tail. It's a guppy fish. It loves to zoom past the dark leaves. We also have black and spotted fish that blend in with the shadows. The Angel fish are usually shy and always hide. But if you'll see one, it's gonna stare back at you without blinking. Seems like it can see through your soul 😂 Sometimes, frogs visit our ponds. They camouflage with the green duckweed. They just pop their eyes out of the water. 😁 It is so relaxing to sit by the water and watch the little fish swim. Every day, there is something new to see in our three little ponds. 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿 🐠 🌿

/>

title.title: Book that impacted me | LOH #285 contest week
title.body: > Hello ladies, I've been a bit busy and out of touch, but this week I took the time to stop by and, since it's World Book Day, I'd like to answer this question:

> Saludos ladies, he estado un poco ocupada y perdida pero esta semana me tomé el tiempo de pasar por aquí y aprovechando que es el Día del Libro para responder esta pregunta:
![IMG_0756.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYuD3TQana4ZRXEn2K62PPQ5qzyDkRnXdyofpRNEK3rJ4/IMG_0756.jpeg)

> > What is one book, YouTube video, movie, or life lesson on self-development that has truly impacted you? It could be about skills, money, purpose, relationships, health, or personal growth. Share what it taught you and why you would recommend it to others. A while ago, when I was feeling a bit lost, I read the book Atomic Habits. It's a book that talks about those things you know you should do but don't. It presents them as four laws you should follow to create good habits: - Make it obvious - Make it appealing - Make it easy - Make it satisfying This system really helps when you're stuck, always saying you should do something but never doing it because you don't feel like it. But really, it's because you don't know how to make the process of achieving your goals enjoyable. We often think that making an effort is suffering, and it doesn't have to be that way. This book is quite flexible. It's not really motivational; rather, it's about helping you optimize your daily actions and turn them into habits. It doesn't force you into extreme changes, but rather into small systems that you can adjust to your liking. And from this, you begin to create a foundation of discipline, but without being overly strict.

> > ¿Cuál es un libro, vídeo de YouTube, película o lección de vida sobre el autodesarrollo que realmente le ha impactado? Podría tratarse de habilidades, dinero, propósito, relaciones, salud o crecimiento personal. Comparte lo que te enseñó y por qué lo recomendarías a otros. Hace tiempo cuando estaba un poco perdida leí el libro de Hábitos Atómicos, es un libro que habla de eso que sabes que debes hacer pero no lo haces. Y te lo plasma como 4 leyes que debes seguir para generar buenos hábitos. - Hacerlo obvio - Hacerlo atractivo - Hacerlo fácil - Hacerlo satisfactorio Este sistema realmente te ayuda cuando estás estancado, en el siempre decir y nunca hacer porque no tienes ganas pero realmente es porque no sabes como hacer que en el proceso para conseguir tus objetivos se vea agradable porque muchas veces pensamos que esforzarnos es sufrir y no tiene porque ser así. Este libro es bastante flexible. No es realmente motivacional, sino trata de que puedas optimizar tus acciones diarias y convertirlas en hábitos. No te obliga a cambios extremos, sino a sistemas pequeños que tú puedes ajustar a tu gusto. Y a partir de esto empiezas a crear una base de disciplina, pero sin ser tan estricta.

title.title: Silent Bloom - Black & White Photography [ENG/ESP]
title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSPLXkAPFaswVhKjptZVDY6Px4xbnUAR9KmYzXPFbovut/20260423_124245.jpg)

Hello friends and community, this little blog will be my entry for 📸 PhotoFeed Contest - Black & White Photography Round 166. I hope you like the photograph I share with you today. It is a photograph I took some time ago and I was eager to share with the community.
> Hola amigos y comunidad, este pequeño blog será mi entrada para 📸 PhotoFeed Contest - Black & White Photography Round 166. Espero que les guste la fotografía que hoy les comparto. Es una fotografía que tomé hace un tiempo y que estaba ansioso por compartir con la comunidad.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXG2WQa24nbqoWaSke2U1ixevpXeWXJxsQSSsk821MTjY/2.png)

I took a photograph of a flower that was very still in the middle of the grass. Its petals are very thin, delicate, and fragile, but still it stands alone against the wind. A single flower surrounded by all kinds of grasses and leaves. I wanted to capture this moment of this flower, just as it is, without adornments or distractions, only its natural form which by itself seems to speak and tell a story. The image is very simple, but in that very simplicity there is a kind of truth that speaks for itself, a reminder that beauty also lies in simplicity. I feel that these flowers are nature's way of always surprising us. Sharing this photo is my way of saying that sometimes we need to stop and simply observe. I chose black and white because it eliminates the noise of color and leaves only the essence of the subject in the photograph. In monochrome, the flower becomes something that is much more than a plant; it becomes a symbol, a form of light and shadows. It gives me that feeling of memory, of textures from the past. I hope you liked my photograph. I can only wish you, as every week, all the luck and success in the world. Bye bye.
> Tomé una fotografía de una flor que estaba muy quieta en medio de la hierba. Sus pétalos son muy finos, delicados y frágiles, pero aun así resiste solitaria el viento. Una única flor rodeada de todo tipo de hierbas y hojas. Quise capturar este momento de esta flor, justo así como es, sin adornos y sin distracciones, solo su forma natural que de por sí sola parece hablar y contar una historia. La imagen es bien simple, pero en esa misma simpleza hay una especie de verdad que por sí sola habla, un recordatorio de que en lo simple está la belleza también. Siento que estas flores son la manera que tiene la naturaleza de siempre sorprendernos. Compartir esta foto es mi manera de decir que a veces necesitamos detenernos y simplemente observar. Elegí el blanco y negro porque elimina el ruido del color y deja solo la esencia del sujeto en la fotografía. En monocromo, la flor se convierte en algo que es mucho más que una planta, se convierte en un símbolo, una forma de luz y sombras. Me da esa sensación de memoria, de texturas del pasado. Espero que les haya gustado mi fotografía. Solo me queda desearles, como cada semana, toda la suerte y éxitos del mundo. Chau chau.

title.title: YAKTAK повернувся до треку \
title.body: Попса теж буває гарною і якісною. Прикладів чудових треків маємо безліч, а серед молодих голосів, мабуть, дуже добре сприймається український виконавець YAKTAK, справжнє ім'я якого - Ярослав Карпук. Виріс він у маленькому селищі на Волині. Своєю наполегливою працею зміг досягти певної популярності та має значний, відомий меломанам, доробок. Голос цього виконавця не сплутаєш ні з ким: оксамитовий бас і відчуття сили та тепла в ньому захопили серця багатьох фанів і особливо фанаток.\nНезважаючи на щільний графік закордонних концертів, YAKTAK продовжує творити. Артист випустив на днях трек не про кохання, а про його сліди у житті. \

— нова пісня Ярослава після тривалої паузи. В ній не знайдете нічого вражаючого: ні гучних приспівів, ні розгорнутої любовної драми. Лише стан людини. Той, який знайомий майже кожному, але який рідко хто може якось назвати.\n\

— це не про кохання з квітами та поцілунками. Вона про момент, що настає після. Коли людини вже немає поруч, але вона досі скрізь: у запаху в салоні авто, у звичці торкатися шиї, у дрібницях, від яких раптово стискається десь усередині.
Це про людей, які йдуть, але не зникають. Про почуття, що не питають дозволу ні увійти, ні лишитись. Трек не розповідає історію — він передає стан. І в цьому його сила: слухач не читає про чиїсь переживання, він одразу впізнає свої.
